With three windows and degree 3 or 5 it returns an underdetermined solution, including negative covariance diagonals; one probe returned a cubic coefficient of 1560 and a covariance diagonal of -2.95e20. casa-rs reduces the fitted degree to the number of valid windows minus one, warns, and pads the requested coefficient/error vectors with zeros. Valid, determined fits retain the requested degree and CASA's covariance convention. The existing singular order-one behavior is retained.

    For exactly determined fits, casacore LSQFit::solve subtracts accumulated moments (sum(w*y*y) - x*b + x*(N*x-b)) and divides by at least one when estimating residual scatter. Roundoff can become a positive uncertainty although the data determine every coefficient exactly. A five-window degree-4 probe returned coefficient 24697.456405169 and uncertainty 0.0038844, and a flux-density error of 6.1e-7. casa-rs retains zero residual uncertainty when there are no residual degrees of freedom, extending its existing two-window linear-fit convention. The oracle separately bounds these CASA artifacts to 1e-3 of the corresponding coefficient/flux scale and checks native zeros; determined coefficients, covariance, and overdetermined uncertainties retain their direct numerical comparisons. Existing stricter order-one checks remain.

    Source: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/SolvableVisCal.cc, SolvableVisJones::fluxscale, coefficient allocation and myfitorder branches. Reproduction: tools/casa-compat/fluxscale_oracle.py builds the three-window input; the negative-order crash must be run in a separate Python process. Regression: casa-calibration's spectral-fit tests and captured CASA gain data.

    Explicit gencal wildcards can index outside the calibration array¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, gencal(vis, caltable, 'amp', antenna='*', parameter=2.0) passes -1 as an antenna index and aborts in ArrayBase. With spw='*' CASA similarly passes a negative window index and segfaults. A negated antenna clause such as A1;!A3 can pass -3 and abort after processing A1.

    For the specified gain, phase, delay and opacity types, casa-rs treats each whole-axis * as that axis's empty selector, which broadcasts the value. It refuses a negative antenna index before publishing the table, preserving any existing product. The paired calibration_gencal_specify_oracle.py compares the wildcard results to CASA's empty selectors and checks safe rejection of the negated clause (#32).

    The legacy antposvla path also aborts with an empty antenna selector when logging an element of the empty antenna array. Casa-rs safely rotates the first offset triple and broadcasts it to all antennas. Explicit antenna selections retain CASA's repeated in-place rotations when the parameter vector cycles. The paired tools/casa-compat/calibration_gencal_antpos_oracle.py checks both forms (#32).

    A one-receptor SYSPOWER shape aborts switched-power calibration¶

    On CASA 6.7.6.14, gencal(caltype='rq') with one receptor per SYSPOWER array aborts in ArrayBase::validateConformance. Casa-rs validates each input shape and raises an error before publishing the calibration table. The switched-power oracle checks the isolated CASA abort and native refusal on the same MeasurementSet (#1535).

    CASA also uses the first scan from an empty selection when a SYSPOWER timestamp falls between visibility scans. The reference case records scan 0. Casa-rs records the calibration table's unknown scan value, -1, and keeps the power sample and its original time.

    Opacity priors can index a nonexistent second receptor¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 constructs a scalar solution for gencal(caltype='opac'). Selecting the second receptor with pol='L' or both with pol='X,Y' terminates the Python process in the calibration array slicer. Casa-rs raises a task error and preserves an existing table. The empty selector, R and X select the scalar value.

    Source: synthesis/MeasurementComponents/SolvableVisCal.cc, SolvableVisCal::specify. The paired tools/casa-compat/calibration_gencal_opacity_oracle.py runs the CASA probes in isolated processes and checks native table preservation (#32).

    Legacy iterative leakage solving can terminate the Python process¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts calibrater.setsolve(type='D') and type='Dgen' with setvi(old=True), then segfaults in solve() on the circular-feed cross-hand fixture. The direct leakage oracle verifies that setup succeeds before each isolated CASA crash. Casa-rs uses its native iterative solver on the same selected dataset, and verifies the solutions, flags and formal errors against CASA's working VI2 path. CASA's DLLS and DfLLS solvers produce tables in both iterators.

    Fluxscale history can contain uninitialized object identifiers¶

    MSHistoryHandler::addMessage writes every required HISTORY column except OBJECT_ID. Repeated CASA 6.7.6.14 fluxscale calls return arbitrary integers there (one run produced -1045601744 and 32549); freshly allocated storage can instead read as zero. casa-rs initializes this required field to zero. The oracle compares all other history content, checks the native zero, and treats the current timestamp and implementation version as process-specific metadata.

    CASA 6.7.6.14 also accepts refspwmap=[] at the Python boundary but indexes element zero unconditionally in SolvableVisJones::fluxscale, causing a segfault. Native empty mapping means identity, as refspwmap=[-1] does.

    Fluxscale listfile can overwrite scientific table files¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 opens listfile with ofstream truncation without checking whether it names a file inside the input MS, input caltable or output product. Such a path can overwrite a scientific table file. Stream failures are also unchecked, so the task can report success without producing the listing. casa-rs refuses overlapping listing/product paths before mutation and reports listing write errors. This preserves data and implements the requested file output rather than silently losing it. Source: SolvableVisJones::fluxscale, the oListFile stream blocks. The direct calibrater writes the listing before publishing or appending to the caltable, so retrying after a listing error does not duplicate rows. The direct oracle checks the pinned success with a directory as the listing path and native preservation of an existing table.

    tablerow.__getitem__ process abort in CASA 6.7.6.14¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, indexing a tablerow accessor via r[rownr] (including valid and out-of-range row indices, e.g. r[0] or r[10]) terminates Python with segmentation fault (signal 11, exit code 139) inside the SWIG casac::tablerow wrapper (__getitem__), even though r.get(rownr) and len(r) succeed.

    casa-rs implements tablerow.__getitem__ safely under the GIL-detached Rust table accessor, supporting negative indices, slices, and sequences of row indices, and raising IndexError cleanly on out-of-range indices. Table tool issue #1028

    table.fromASDM can report success after discarding XML values¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, call table().fromASDM("out.table", "Scan.xml") with <ScanTable><row><scanNumber>12</scanNumber></row></ScanTable>. The table contains one row but its scanNumber is 0. The legacy SAX code only enables its value callback for fields listed in a working directory file named taglist.txt; even with the tag in that file, this build did not store the value. With a nonexistent XML file CASA returns True and creates no table.

    casa-rs uses the same ordered column descriptions and converts the XML values directly. It reports invalid or unreadable input before replacing the destination. The ASDM XML converter reads one table at a time; it does not import ASDM datasets or their binary data. See #1028.

    FITS TNULL cards can disappear from table.fromfits output¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 preserved the integer -32768 in a FITS 1J column but did not add a NULL column keyword for its TNULL2 = -32768 card. FITSTabular::nullsFromHDU looks up each indexed card with a zero-based column index. casa-rs preserves both the unscaled integer cell and the matching null marker so readers can interpret it. See #1028.

    The Python callibrary reader executes calibration-library file contents¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 builds and executes a Python statement from each record line in casatasks.private.callibrary.callibrary.read. A file can run arbitrary Python in the calling process. The casa-rs helper accepts the historical record literals and rejects executable expressions. It clears any partial records and reports the line using the malformed-library error path.

    Callibrary joint scan maps mark other observations unavailable¶

    • Date noted: 2026-11-17
    • Status: corrected under the standing evident-intent rule (#1518)
    • Affected code: CASA 6.7.6.14 CLPatchPanel MS constructor, missing-scan catch.

    With scan 1 in observation 0 and scan 2 in observation 1 in both the MS and G table, obsmap='self' scanmap='self' skips all calibration. The constructor tries each requested scan within each calibration observation. When a scan is absent in the current observation, it calls recordBadMSIndices(reqMSobs, theseMSscan, ...), marking that scan bad in every requested observation, including the observation where the scan exists. With an existing corrected column, CASA leaves its values and weights unchanged; ordinary calflag adds no flags. This contradicts the explicitly independent observation/scan maps.

    casa-rs checks availability within the actual joint mapped context and calibrates its valid buffers. The public task oracle retains the raw CASA result and compares native output to an independent CASA control with two explicit library slices, obs='0' scan='1' and obs='1' scan='2', retaining both self maps and the identical input MS/calibration table. That control matches native corrected data, flags and weight/sigma columns. Missing joint contexts still use the ordinary unavailable-calibration rules. No tolerance is relaxed, and this correction is separate from same-input task matches.

    Gaincal can crash while opening a tracked virtual image¶

    On Linux, CASA 6.7.6.14 saved a virtual GridFT image with tclean(phasecenter='TRACKFIELD', savemodel='virtual') on an MS with an attached Uranus ephemeris. Calling gaincal on that MS terminated Python with signal 11. CASA wrote a nonconstant prediction to MODEL_DATA when savemodel='modelcolumn' used the same image settings and visibilities.

    casa-rs reads the saved source, tracking epoch and image direction and evaluates the tracked prediction in the visibility buffer. The gaincal_oracle.py --case ephemeris fixture compares native gains and downstream application from the virtual image to CASA gains and application from its scratch prediction. It also covers a tracked mosaic, an external ephemeris table and moving-field parallactic angles. See #30.

    Empty or ragged nested sequences in quantity records crash or corrupt values¶

    • Date noted: 2026-11-18
    • Status: CASA crashes or truncates/zero-pads data; casa-rs refuses the inputs (#1170).
    • Affected code: casatools Python-to-Variant / QuantumHolder record conversion.

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, qa.quantity({'value': [[]], 'unit': 'm'}) terminates Python with a segmentation fault (exit code 139). For ragged nested floating-point lists, CASA silently discards trailing elements in longer rows ([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0]] becomes array([[1.], [3.]])) or zero-pads shorter rows ([[1.0], [2.0, 3.0]] becomes array([[1., 0.], [2., 3.]])).

    casa-rs checks nesting depth and row shapes in crates/casars-python/src/convert.rs and rejects empty or ragged nested Python sequences with CASA's catchable Illegal Quantum record in QuantumHolder::fromRecord RuntimeError instead of crashing or corrupting values (#1252, #1170).

    Component record imports announce Stokes but store an unknown polarization¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 cl.add and cl.fromrecord accept a flux record with four values and no polarisation or error field. FluxRep::fromRecord logs "Using the default of Stokes", then overwrites that default with its local UNKNOWN_POLARISATION enumerator. getcomponent consequently reports polarisation='Unknown'. A real-valued error vector instead makes the import fail because the local enumerator is still unknown.

    casa-rs retains the announced Stokes basis for accepted records, preserving all four flux values. It preserves CASA's rejection of the real error-vector form. This avoids storing an unusable polarization label or losing the component's numerical values. The correction follows the standing owner rule in AGENTS.md for behavior that contradicts CASA's evident intent; there is no new owner exclusion.

    Evidence: tools/simulation/componentlist_record_spectra_oracle.py, casa_componentlist_record_spectra.json (missing_pol_no_error), and test_componentlist_records.py (#1252).

    Gaussian component record imports abort on invalid axes or position angles¶

    CASA 6.7.6-14 cl.add(record) terminates the process with SIGABRT when a Gaussian record has zero or negative axes, a minor axis longer than its major axis, or a position angle outside ±360 degrees. GaussianShape::fromRecord constructs the shape before rejecting these values, and its constructor's AlwaysAssert(ok()) escapes the tool boundary.

    casa-rs rejects the invalid component with a catchable RuntimeError before appending it. Valid components retain CASA's geometry and position-angle normalization. This follows the standing rule to correct CASA crashes; callers retain their existing list and Python session. The isolated CASA subprocess receipts are in crates/casars-python/python/tests/data/casa_componentlist_record_validation.json, regenerated by tools/simulation/componentlist_record_validation_oracle.py.

    Duplicated imstat axes crash CASA¶

    • Date noted: 2026-11-18
    • Status: CASA aborts; casa-rs refuses the request (#977).
    • Affected code: casatools image statistics, ImageStatsCalculator::statistics.

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, imstat(imagename, axes=[0, 0]) aborts the Python process (SIGABRT, exit 134) inside the statistics calculation; the same happens for any duplicated axis. An out-of-range or negative axis is refused with the catchable Invalid cursor axes: [4]. instead, so the crash on duplicates is an uncontrolled path, not a policy.

    casa-rs refuses a duplicated axis with Invalid cursor axes: [0, 0]: an axis is named twice; CASA 6.7.6.14 aborts on it (crates/casa-images/src/analysis.rs, parse_axes), keeping every other axes form CASA accepts, including the minimum-forms -1 for all axes (#977).

    Replacing one Multi-MS model can remove another partition's Fourier grid¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, split an MS with partition(separationaxis='baseline', numsubms=2), then write an image with ft(mms, field='0', model=...). The two physical SOURCE records can name the same Fourier image. Replacing the model on the first partition removes that image. A subsequent uvsub on the other partition fails to open the image its record names.

    casa-rs gives independent SOURCE or MAIN records their own Fourier grids. Replacing one record leaves the other partition's grid and recipe readable in CASA and casa-rs. Replacement also preserves retired grids in SOURCE. SOURCE does not identify every MAIN that can still name an older grid, including a MAIN with stale metadata after a failed write. A replacement can remove a retired grid in its own MAIN directory after checking the current model records. The standalone calibration_ft_oracle.py fixture exercises the replacement sequence.

    TaQL derived geometry treats an ephemeris field offset as a direction¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 msmetadata.phasecenter(field, epoch) follows the attached body and applies the field offset. The TaQL mscal.hadec1() and mscal.azel1() functions use the stored PHASE_DIR directly for the same field. For the Uranus fixture, mscal.hadec1() reports a declination of 0.00190 rad while the attached phase centre is near 0.20677 rad.

    The calibration engine and diagnostics read the attached direction at the requested epoch. The calibration_ephemeris_geometry_oracle.py fixture obtains the per-epoch phase centres from CASA and evaluates CASA geometry on fixed snapshots of those directions (#989).

    Rejected Tsys weight initialization can leave empty spectra¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 can add WEIGHT_SPECTRUM and SIGMA_SPECTRUM to a MeasurementSet before rejecting initweights(wtmode='tsys', dowtsp=True) with an invalid gainfield or interpolation setting. On that failure the new columns have undefined cells and the original weights are unchanged.

    casa-rs validates the setup before it creates either column, so a rejected call leaves the original spectrum schema available for retry. The paired calibration_initweights_tsys_oracle.py cases cover both setup errors and the unchanged weight, sigma and flag values (#1524).

    The public calibrater.initweights('ones', spwmap=None) call can also set every weight to one before raising SystemError. casa-rs rejects the malformed window map before updating any columns. The direct-tool oracle checks both outcomes (#1524).

    immath(mode="pola") crashes with UnboundLocalError on unitless polithresh¶

    • Date noted: 2026-11-18
    • Status: CASA crashes with an uncaught Python UnboundLocalError; casa-rs accepts unitless thresholds in image brightness units (#977).
    • Affected code: casatasks/private/task_immath.py, _immath_new_pola.

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, when mode="pola" and polithresh is given without a unit (e.g. polithresh="0.1"), _immath_new_pola skips creating the temporary linear-polarization image lpol because if (myqa.getunit(polithresh) != ""): wraps both unit conversion and mypo.linpolint(..., outfile=lpol), yet the later if (polithresh): block unconditionally evaluates lpol and raises UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'lpol'.

    casa-rs parses polithresh as an optional-unit quantity (crates/casa-images/src/analysis/immath/pol.rs), treats a unitless polithresh as already expressed in the input image's brightness unit, and thresholds linear polarized intensity normally (#977).

    immath polarization debiasing ignores non-conforming sigma units¶

    • Date noted: 2026-11-18
    • Status: CASA silently corrupts/masks output; casa-rs rejects non-conforming or missing units when the image carries a brightness unit (#977).
    • Affected code: casatools/casacore quantity conversion in task_immath.py, _immath_new_poli.

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, _immath_new_poli converts a positive sigma via myqa.convert(qsigma, iunit) and reads .getvalue() without verifying that sigma's unit conforms to the input image's bunit (for example passing sigma="1K" or unitless sigma="10" on a "Jy/beam" image). On mismatch qa.convert leaves the value/unit invalid so downstream imagepol debiasing silently over-thresholds and masks the entire output plane.

    casa-rs validates unit conformance via get_conformant_value when sigma > 0 (crates/casa-images/src/analysis/immath/pol.rs) and refuses non-conforming or unitless sigma against non-empty image bunit with a clear error (#977).

    Median fringe smoothing wraps delay values as phase¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, smoothcal(smoothtype='median') on a Fringe Jones calibration table applies phase wrapping to every FPARAM component. The condition ipar == 0 || 4 in FringeJones::smooth is always true. A valid 8 ns delay therefore became about 1.717 ns in a window with only that sample. The same branch also skips the median filter for delays and dispersive delays.

    casa-rs wraps only the two phase parameters and applies the numerical median to the delay, rate, and dispersive delay parameters. The use of fringe rates for predicting phase wraps and the phase outputs follow CASA (#1525).

    Re-referencing a delay table crashes CASA¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, rerefant(refantmode='strict', refant='A0') terminates the process when the input is a K Jones delay table. SolvableVisJones::applyRefAnt reads CPARAM before dispatching on the table type. Delay tables use FPARAM, and only Fringe overrides the reference calculation for real-valued parameters.

    casa-rs raises a task error for unsupported table types before publishing a result. The paired oracle runs this CASA check in a child process (#1525).

    statwt creates spectra then fails on an explicitly selected subset¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 initializes a required WEIGHT_SPECTRUM or SIGMA_SPECTRUM column for the original MS when chanbin requests channel bins. When the selected table predates the new column, CASA then raises a RuntimeError and asks the caller to rerun the selection. The first call writes the initial spectrum across the MS and leaves the original flags and scalar columns intact.

    casa-rs initializes the physical MAIN tables and subsequently applies statistical weights to the requested rows in one call. Unselected rows retain the spectrum obtained by expanding their original scalar values. The paired fixture compares this result with CASA's documented two-call sequence and checks unselected rows (#1524).

    Column statistics change when the same NaN moves between rows¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 derives table.statistics and calstat quantiles from an ordering that includes NaN. The rows [0, 3, 1, NaN, 4, 8, 9] gave a finite interquartile range of 7 and a NaN median. Moving that NaN to the start gave an interquartile range of 8, a median of 3 and NaN for both bounds. The sum and variance were NaN in each case.

    casa-rs returns deterministic bounds from the non-NaN samples, counts all samples and returns NaN for the moments and quantiles when a NaN makes those quantities undefined. This preserves the existing native table tool behavior in the public calibration task (#1526).

    Accumulating a bandpass updates a fraction of the Jones cells¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14's calibrater.accumulate is available with setvi(old=True). In the paired eight-channel B Jones fixture it changed 20 of 160 valid complex cells. At each of two solution times, only the first five channels of antenna 0 received the Jones product. The other valid factors remained as they were.

    casa-rs multiplies the per-receptor, per-channel factors for every antenna. The analytic self-accumulation check squares all 160 valid factors and checks flags separately (#1525).

    Accumulation depends on the physical order of overlapping field times¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, the old accumulation method passes the incremental table's time column to CTTimeInterp1. The interpolator uses binary search on those times. Physically grouping rows by field can leave that column out of chronological order when time ranges overlap.

    CASA changed valid gains when the paired fixture was sorted by time. casa-rs orders its time series before interpolation and matches the time-ordered CASA control. It preserves the prior numerical payload at flagged cells. In a selected gain-field comparison, CASA replaced one flagged payload with complex unity. The flags and valid values matched (#1525).

    Selecting a field in simultaneous calibration rows modifies other fields¶

    The old CASA 6.7.6.14 accumulation method groups rows by spectral window and time. It uses the first row's FIELD_ID to decide whether to modify the entire group. In a fixture that divides antenna solutions at the same timestamp between two fields, selecting FLUX also changes PHASE rows. Selecting PHASE skips all the rows.

    casa-rs applies the correction within each selected field. The paired fixture checks the product on every eligible row and checks the unselected rows byte for byte (#1525).

    Accumulation repairs a legacy input even when a separate output is requested¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14's old accumulation path upgrades a pre-4.1 cumulative table when it opens the source. The paired input lost its original schema: CASA added OBSERVATION_ID and OBSERVATION before publishing the requested separate product.

    casa-rs applies the same legacy upgrade inside the output snapshot. The result matches the upgraded CASA product and a separately named original retains its legacy schema (#1525).

    Accumulation can terminate during contextual time interpolation¶

    With the old CASA 6.7.6.14 visibility iterator, accumulation terminated the process on the test fixtures for spline and linearperscan. linearperobs completed when there was one observation and terminated on the two-observation probe.

    casa-rs uses the calibration application's time interpolator with the cumulative rows' scan and observation metadata. In local comparisons, the per-scan output matched two independent single-field CASA controls. An independent SciPy natural spline matched 52 valid complex factors in the spline comparison (#1525).

    The public calibrater.accumulate(t=None) call can leave a Python conversion error pending and terminate CASA 6.7.6.14. casa-rs raises TypeError before touching the input or output table (#1525).

    Image record restore can crash or damage an existing output¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 segfaults in ia.fromrecord if an otherwise valid image record has an empty outer coordsys record. A native restore of a record with a two-axis coordinate system and shape=[2, 3, 2] throws Failed AlwaysAssert setCoordinateInfo after replacing the output with an unreadable directory. Casa-rs reports both errors in Python and preserves the prior native image and its history (#1625).

    Direct image methods and gzip-compressed FITS¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 reads gzip-compressed FITS through image.fromfits and image.newimagefromfits. The same file raises an unable-to-open error in open, newimage, newimagefromfile, fromimage, and newimagefromimage.

    casa-rs also accepts these files through the direct FITS attachment and copy methods. They preserve the FITS pixels, blank mask, coordinates, unit, and history through CFITSIO. The explicit import methods agree with CASA. See #1625.

    A FITS attachment can report a different name after an environment change¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, open $IMAGE_DIR/source.fits and change IMAGE_DIR to another directory containing a different source.fits. The attached image continues reading from the first file. image.name() reports the second path. casa-rs keeps the attachment name and pixel reads tied to the resolved input from the original open. #1625

    Named image creation can overwrite a lexical destination without permission¶

    With left/alias pointing to right/nested, create left/product.im and leave right/product.im absent. In CASA 6.7.6.14, image.fromshape("left/alias/../product.im", shape=[2, 3]) can replace left/product.im with the default overwrite=False. CASA checks the path through the symlink for a collision, then creates the image at the lexical path. casa-rs checks both paths and preserves the existing product unless overwrite is enabled. #1625

    An unbraced environment variable at the end of a path can duplicate the directory¶

    With IMAGE_FILE=source.fits, CASA 6.7.6.14 can open /dir/${IMAGE_FILE} while /dir/$IMAGE_FILE fails with a missing-file error. Casacore's path expansion can repeat the preceding directory components when it finds the unbraced variable in a later component. casa-rs opens the same source.fits with either spelling. #1625

    A bracketed FITS attachment can read a different file from the supplied path¶

    Place distinct valid FITS images at source.fits and source.fits[0]. In CASA 6.7.6.14, image.open("source.fits[0]") requires the bracketed file to exist, then reports and reads source.fits. Both explicit import methods read the literal bracketed file. casa-rs consistently treats brackets as part of the filename and uses whichhdu for explicit HDU selection. #1625

    FITS import can abort on an empty primary HDU¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 aborts in ia.fromfits(infile=path, whichhdu=0) when the FITS primary HDU has NAXIS=0 and a later extension contains the image. The same file imports successfully when whichhdu=-1 selects the first image or whichhdu=1 selects its extension. casa-rs returns RuntimeError for the empty HDU and accepts both ways to select the extension. See #1625.

    importfits can remove an existing image before import succeeds¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 removes imagename as soon as it sees overwrite=True. A subsequent validation error, such as a beam whose major axis is smaller than its minor axis, leaves the old image gone. A beam position angle given in time units can fail after publishing the replacement image. The task and both explicit image methods (fromfits and newimagefromfits) also delete the output path early when it contains the input FITS file. casa-rs stages the native image and exchanges it only after the new product is complete. It refuses output paths containing the FITS input and nonempty directories that are not native images (#977, #1625).

    exportfits drops characters when wrapping long HISTORY cards¶

    • Date noted: 2026-11-19
    • Status: CASA silently loses history text; casa-rs wraps losslessly (#977).
    • Affected code: casacore ImageFITSConverter FITS HISTORY card continuation writer.

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, exportfits(..., history=True) wraps logtable lines across 80-byte FITS HISTORY cards by placing 72 characters on the first card and > followed by 71 characters on continuation cards, but skips character index 143 on card 3 and subsequent continuation cards when the wrapped line spans more than 143 characters. On cube_i.im (crates/casa-images/tests/data/exportfits/cube_i.im), CASA drops 'y' from csys={...} in the 202-character ia.fromshape(...) message and drops the closing ')' of the 144-character ia.setrestoringbeam(...) message (emitting 47 HISTORY cards instead of 48); on a synthetic 160-digit "0123..." history entry, CASA drops '3' at index 143 between >...012 and >456....

    casa-rs (crates/casa-images/src/analysis/exportfits.rs, wrap_fits_history_text) splits at 72 characters on the first card and > plus 71 characters on each continuation card without skipping characters, emitting all 48 cards on cube_i.im so both casa-rs and CASA 6.7.6.14 ia.history(list=False) read back all 17 original history entries intact (#977).

    Duplicate immoments requests can leave a partial set of images¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 writes the first output directory for a repeated moment number before the second occurrence reports that the same directory already exists. For example, moments=[0,0] leaves the .integrated directory after a failed task. casa-rs checks the destination names before writing and refuses the duplicate without publishing a product (#977).

    imsubimage aborts for an out-of-range keepaxes index¶

    On a four-axis image, CASA 6.7.6.14 aborts the process with itsAxes(i) >= naxes for imsubimage(dropdeg=True, keepaxes=[4]). The check is in casacore's AxesSpecifier::apply. casa-rs returns an out-of-range error before creating or replacing the output image. With dropdeg=False, CASA and casa-rs ignore keepaxes.

    The same abort occurs with the image tool's ia.subimage(dropdeg=True, keepaxes=[5]) on a three-axis image. The shared casa-rs selection returns a Python RuntimeError and leaves any existing output intact.

    An image subimage can replace its source history table¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 can replace the source image's logtable when that path is passed to ia.subimage(overwrite=True). The source history then fails to read because the table lacks the TIME column. If the history table is already open, CASA reports that it is in the table cache. Casa-rs rejects overwriting existing entries inside the source image before staging the cutout. The same replacement through ia.fromimage or ia.newimagefromimage succeeds in CASA and leaves the source history unreadable. Casa-rs protects the source before staging either copy.

    Paged image concatenation can remove a source image or mask¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts imageconcat(overwrite=True) with an existing output directory that contains an input. It removes the nested image before failing to read its pixels. Replacing an input's mask subtable as the output can also succeed, leaving the input mask unreadable because the new table has no PagedArray column. Casa-rs raises a Python error before either replacement. A new output directory inside a source image is supported when no existing subtable is replaced.

    imsubimage permutes coordinate labels after dropping transposed axes¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, take a cube in RA, Dec, Stokes, frequency order and apply imtrans(order="3012"). Then run imsubimage(box="1,2,4,5", chans="2", stokes="Q", dropdeg=True, keepaxes=[0]). The resulting shape is [1, 4, 4], with pixels in frequency, RA, Dec order. CASA labels the axes Dec, frequency, RA. In CoordinateUtil::dropRemovedAxes, the permutation passed to CoordinateSystem::transpose maps from creation order to pixel order, while transpose expects the inverse. casa-rs keeps the coordinates on their original pixel axes as it removes Stokes.

    plotbandpass passes a fractional platforming channel to range¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 raises TypeError while checking a wide bandpass for platforming. The check computes the two interior channel offsets with floating-point division, then passes those offsets to Python range(). The paired 64-channel fixture enters this branch.

    casa-rs evaluates the check at integer channel indices. In the fixture, a step at channel 32 produces a platforming report at the 10 percent threshold and a clean result at the 100 percent threshold (#1526).

    PlotMS disabling selection calls the selection setter with a missing argument¶

    The installed CASA PlotMS wrapper raises Exception("updateImmediately must be a boolean") for selectdata=False. The wrapper's no-selection call omits a selector argument before the update flag. casa-rs applies the requested unfiltered selection and leaves the caller's selector expressions inactive (#1526).

    plotbandpass references an undefined name when WEATHER is absent¶

    An atmospheric overlay on the paired bandpass with no associated WEATHER table raises NameError in CASA 6.7.6.14 when it tries to read needToClose_mymsmd. casa-rs evaluates the native atmospheric profile with the station defaults and plots the original calibration spectra with the resulting curve (#1526).

    Listing an incomplete antenna integration can terminate CASA¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14's listcal reshapes each spectral window's solution rows into complete antenna integrations. Removing the last antenna row from an otherwise regular G Jones table terminated the paired CASA subprocess after opening the requested listing file.

    casa-rs validates the antenna blocks before publishing a listing. The same input raises a recoverable error and leaves the destination absent. Complete integrations retain their original order, even when two have the same time and field (#1526).

    Beam removal can delete metadata before rejecting a record¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, ia.setrestoringbeam(remove=True, beam={'junk': 2}) on a native image with a restoring beam raises RuntimeError because the record has no major field. Reopening the image shows the beam was already removed. The call validates the record while preparing history after deleting the beam, even when history is disabled.

    casa-rs validates the supplied record before it saves any changes, so a rejected call preserves the restoring beam and history. See #1625.

    Naming a removed coordinate axis can terminate CASA¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 can terminate when coordsys.setnames is called with type="linear" and two names for a linear coordinate whose world and pixel maps are [0, -2]. casa-rs raises RuntimeError before applying either name. Passing the one visible axis name without a coordinate type renames that axis and preserves the stored removed-axis name (#1626).

    Time averaging LAG_DATA and mixed FLOAT_DATA loses visibility information¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 leaves LAG_DATA undefined while time averaging, and a LAG_DATA-only product can also have undefined FLAG cells and zero spectral weights. The native average retains the lag axis. It averages defined lag values using scalar weights, preferring rows with an unflagged frequency sample for the same correlation. It computes the frequency flags and statistics from the input frequency cells.

    With datacolumn="all" on a MeasurementSet containing both FLOAT_DATA and complex visibilities, VbAvg::accumulateElementForCubes can accumulate calibrated and single-dish weights into the same buffer. The resulting denominators attenuate CORRECTED_DATA, MODEL_DATA, and FLOAT_DATA. The same layout can substitute FLOAT_DATA for complex DATA. Native averaging uses the calibrated weights for corrected and model samples and the observed variance for DATA and FLOAT_DATA. The oracle verifies the independent lanes against CASA runs on the separate layouts and against an analytic lag sum. Owner decision

    SPW-partitioned mstransform can drop a channel qualifier from a window range¶

    With createmms=True, separationaxis='spw', and spw='0~1:1~5', CASA 6.7.6.14 can retain every channel in both windows. Its partition helper matches each numeric window to expressions with a literal window ID and drops the channel qualifier on the range. casa-rs resolves the complete selector and writes channels 1 through 5 for both windows.

    Automatic Multi-MS partitioning can keep flagged rows with keepflags disabled¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 can publish automatic or baseline Multi-MS members containing rows with FLAG_ROW=true when the task uses keepflags=False. Its worker prepends the flag predicate to an OR-separated partition expression without parenthesizing the partition expression. Later alternatives can bypass the flag predicate. casa-rs selects the partition and applies the flag filter to every row. The paired Multi-MS probe includes an input with every row flagged.

    A nonzero mstransform DDI start can leave dangling row references¶

    With CASA 6.7.6.14, a standalone mstransform(ddistart=3) of an MS with one selected data description writes MAIN rows with DATA_DESC_ID=3 while the DATA_DESCRIPTION table contains one row. That offset is intended for subsequent Multi-MS assembly. The native task publishes the requested MAIN IDs and reserves the preceding data-description entries as flagged rows with valid spectral window and polarization references. The native output remains readable as a standalone MeasurementSet (#1615).

    Channel-width argument variants can crash both MeasurementSet tasks¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 split and mstransform leave a partial MeasurementSet after crashing on a zero-dimensional NumPy integer array or an active width list with a zero or negative width. mstransform also crashes on an empty chanbin list when chanaverage=True.

    The native tasks interpret a zero-dimensional integer array as its scalar value. They reject invalid active lists before creating output. The public channel-averaging oracle runs the crash cases in separate processes and checks the native outcomes. Owner approval

    Channel averaging can leave the weights of FLOAT_DATA or LAG_DATA undefined¶

    With only FLOAT_DATA or LAG_DATA selected, the CASA 6.7.6.14 channel-averaging writer can leave required WEIGHT and SIGMA cells undefined. The spectral statistics writer branches on DATA, CORRECTED_DATA and MODEL_DATA.

    The native tasks derive defined weights and sigmas from calibrated input weights and channel flags. LAG_DATA retains its independent lag axis. The channel-averaging oracle checks the derived numbers against the input. Owner approval

    The same spectral statistics writer is used with mstransform(hanning=True). The native task retains defined WEIGHT and SIGMA using the calibrated noise and the Hanning coefficients. It smooths FLOAT_DATA on the frequency axis and preserves LAG_DATA on its independent axis (#1618).

    Regridding FLOAT_DATA likewise leaves those cells undefined in CASA. The native regrid uses the selected calibrated noise spectrum and the output flags for the scalar reductions (#1618).

    A terminal channel stride can leave an incomplete SPECTRAL_WINDOW¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts mstransform(spw="0:0~8^2", hanning=True) on a nine-channel MS, but its SPW writer attempts to use channel nine when computing the last stride's footprint. It logs an error and leaves the SPW metadata incomplete. The native transform uses the available final channel as the last footprint and writes metadata for all five selected channels (#1618).

    Spectral-window combination can ignore weights when exposures differ¶

    For simultaneous overlapping windows with unequal EXPOSURE, CASA 6.7.6.14 mstransform(combinespws=True) reports that it will use spectral weights. MSTransformManager::combineCubeOfData modifies a local coefficient during its first pass but reloads the original geometric coefficient when it adds the visibility. With equal bandwidth and observed weights of 4/9 and 4, overlapping real samples 16 and 1000 yield 508. The native task applies the matching observed weights in the sum and normalization, giving 901.6. Both tasks record the mean input exposure (#1618).

    Combining spectral windows can copy the last row's FLAG_ROW¶

    With simultaneous windows whose row flags disagree, CASA 6.7.6.14 mstransform(combinespws=True) can mark a usable combined row flagged when the last input row is flagged. The loop in MSTransformManager::mapAndAverageVector never increments its count, so the branch that combines flags with AND is skipped. The native task marks the row flagged only if all participating rows are flagged (#1618).

    When spectral windows are combined, CASA also leaves the input's category flags undefined and can leave an association to a deleted spectral window. The native task preserves category flags through the channel mapping and removes associations between windows that no longer exist separately. It refuses to combine distinct LAG_DATA cells when requested, since a merged frequency window has no mapping for their independent lag grids (#1618).

    Regridding can read beyond a final partial averaging bin¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, an odd channel count with chanaverage=True, a two-channel bin and regridms=True leaves a one-sample bin before interpolation. MSTransformManager::average iterates over all output bins using the full bin width, reaching past the input on the final bin. With Hanning enabled, this can change the neighbouring channel's visibility and noise. The native task averages only samples present in the final bin. The paired regridding oracle also checks that result against independent inverse-variance averaging, smoothing and linear interpolation (#1618).

    Channel-bounds regridding can read past the upper band edge¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 can publish a fictitious 0 Hz channel after mstransform(regridms=True, mode='channel_b', start=7, nchan=3, width=1) on a nine-channel ascending input. Its upper-bound check admits index nine even though the last channel is index eight. The native task clips the bounds to the available channels. The oracle checks the native result against a CASA request for the two valid channels (#1618).

    Frame conversion after time averaging can use an unrelated input epoch¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 MSTransformManager::initFrequencyTransGrid reads the selected input's TIME column using the current visibility buffer's row ID. After time averaging, AveragingTvi2 generates output row IDs sequentially, so those IDs no longer identify contributing input rows. In the paired 20-second averaging case, the next group begins at input time +20 seconds but CASA reads the integration at +10 seconds. The native task uses the first contributing input row's epoch. The paired case compares flags exactly and checks values at the project's 0.001 normalized RMS tolerance (#1618).

    Splitting a regridded spectrum can write oversized noise spectra¶

    With nine channels and mstransform(regridms=True, nspw=2), CASA 6.7.6.14 writes SPWs of five and four channels. The noise spectra in the shorter window are padded to five with weight zero and sigma −1. When all samples in that window are flagged, the padding also enters the scalar statistic. The native task writes four values for every channel-indexed column and computes statistics from those four values. It rejects partitions that would leave an empty final window before creating output. CASA can abort when attempting that final slice (#1618).

    Selecting defined spectra or several channel ranges can crash channel averaging¶

    Both CASA 6.7.6.14 tasks can terminate with SIGSEGV and leave an incomplete MS when physical row zero has undefined weight spectra and the selection starts with defined spectra. The output structure checks the physical first row for spectral columns, and the writer checks the first selected row.

    An active per-SPW width vector can also crash when an expression selects more than one channel range in a window. The upstream data handler compares the number of widths with the number of ranges, even when the vector covers every selected window.

    The native tasks allocate output columns for the selected spectra and apply the requested width to each selected SPW. The oracle verifies both crashes in subprocesses and compares native products against equivalent CASA selections. Owner approval

    Transforming an MS with FLOAT_DATA can replace the requested complex DATA¶

    For an input with separately populated DATA and FLOAT_DATA, CASA 6.7.6.14 can fill output DATA from FLOAT_DATA, with zero imaginary components, when the requested layout includes DATA. This occurs with datacolumn="all", "float_data,data", and "lag_data,data" in the physical layout oracle.

    The native tasks select each requested physical column and preserve its own values through row, channel, and correlation selection (#1614).

    Transforming LAG_DATA leaves its cells undefined¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 creates the LAG_DATA descriptor for split and mstransform but the visibility writer skips the column. Selecting only LAG_DATA can also leave FLAG cells undefined.

    The native tasks preserve the selected rows and correlations of LAG_DATA with its independent lag axis. The frequency-channel selection applies to the visibility and flag columns on the spectral axis (#1614).

    Transforming all columns can crash an MS with one scratch column¶

    On an MS with a single physical visibility column, either CORRECTED_DATA or MODEL_DATA, CASA 6.7.6.14 split(datacolumn="all") and mstransform(datacolumn="all") terminate Python with SIGSEGV in the pinned Linux build.

    The native tasks keep the original visibility column and its weights in these sparse layouts (#1614).

    Image removal can delete an open table through a symbolic link¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, open a native image by its table path with table.open(). image.removefile() refuses to delete that path while the table is open. Calling it with a symbolic link to the same path can succeed and remove both the link and the table. The open table handle then refers to a deleted table.

    casa-rs resolves aliases before checking whether the table is in use and preserves both names when it refuses removal. After the last handle closes, removing through the link deletes the link and table as CASA does. See #1625.

    When table.open() holds the native image's logtable, CASA can also remove the parent image and its log. casa-rs checks live subtables before deleting the image.

    An external directory move can also leave an attached tool pointing at a pathname that now contains another image. CASA can delete that replacement image through ia.remove(). casa-rs checks the directory identity captured at open and refuses the removal if the pathname was rebound.

    When a symbolic link lies inside a read-only directory, CASA can delete the linked image and leave the link dangling. casa-rs checks that directory before deleting the image and preserves both entries when it refuses.

    Image rename can move an open table before failing to reattach¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, open one native image in two image tools in the same process and call rename() on the first tool. CASA can move the table, then raise RuntimeError while reopening it under the new name. The second tool keeps the old name and can abort while closing that stale handle. casa-rs refuses the move before changing either path while another tool holds the image. See #1625.

    A lazy imagecalc result provides another reproduction. CASA 6.7.6.14 permits renaming the native operand while the result is attached. Its next pixel read fails because the original tile path no longer exists. casa-rs retains the operand while the lazy result is open and refuses the rename before moving either path.

    When a native table moves across filesystems, CASA 6.7.6.14 copies it and then deletes the original entries in place. If a child directory is readable but denies deletion of its contents, CASA raises after copying the image and can leave a partial table at the original name. casa-rs moves the original table to a private staging directory before copying, keeps the published image readable, and reports the staging path if cleanup fails. See #1625.

    With parent/source.im attached, calling ia.rename("parent", overwrite=True) can delete the source table and unrelated files in parent before CASA 6.7.6.14 reports an error. The same loss occurs when parent is itself a native image table. casa-rs rejects the relationship before deleting either path. The failed call closes the attachment as CASA does. See #1625.

    When a rename destination contains a symbolic link followed by .., CASA 6.7.6.14 can move a native table or FITS file into the directory reached through the link, then remove .. lexically and fail to reopen the image from a different directory. casa-rs refuses the destination before moving the source when the two directory paths resolve differently. It also refuses a destination ending in .. because the argument does not identify a named replacement entry. See #1625.

    MIRIAD directory rename and replaced source paths¶

    With parent/source.mir attached, ia.rename("parent", overwrite=True) in CASA 6.7.6.14 can delete the source image and other entries in parent before reporting an error. casa-rs rejects the ancestor destination before moving or removing either path. The failed call detaches the tool, as in CASA.

    Open source.mir without reading a pixel, move its directory to saved.mir, and create a different image at source.mir. CASA can read the replacement pixels through the original attachment's coordinates. ia.rename("target.mir") can also move the replacement directory. casa-rs checks the image entry it originally opened, so the first pixel read and the rename report that the entry has changed. Both images stay at their existing names. A peer that has already read a pixel keeps its original stream after a rename, as in CASA.

    For moves across filesystems, casa-rs checks that it can remove the original tree before publishing the copy. A directory with readable contents whose permissions prevent removal causes a refusal with both public names preserved. See #1955.

    Copying a MIRIAD image with incomplete coordinates can leave a partial table¶

    Open a MIRIAD image whose header describes fewer coordinate axes than its stored shape, for example two Stokes planes whose MIRIAD codes both map to fractional linear polarization. CASA 6.7.6.14 reports the shape and decoded coordinates, but a named fromimage call creates a partial native table before raising Failed AlwaysAssert setCoordinateInfo. casa-rs reports the shape and decoded coordinates and rejects the copy before publication. See #1955.

    Moving a concatenation can rebind MIRIAD data links¶

    Set source/a.mir/image to the relative symbolic link ../b.mir/image. Concatenate source/a.mir with a different b.mir, using mode="move". CASA 6.7.6.14 can resolve the link to the newly adjacent b.mir and return its pixels in both sections without reporting an error. Casa-rs checks the projected bindings of the linked payload and metadata before moving either input. If a binding would change, the call preserves both inputs and any previous output. mode="copy" preserves the linked file contents in the owned MIRIAD copy. See #1625.

    A failed nested concatenation lock can retain a table lock¶

    Nest a virtual concatenation containing a MIRIAD image and a native table inside another virtual concatenation, with tempclose=False at both levels. Unlock the outer image and take a read lock on its final native member in another process. CASA 6.7.6.14 returns False from lock(writelock=True) but can retain the write lock on the earlier native table. Casa-rs restores each member's physical lease independently of the MIRIAD advisory flags. See #1625.

    A virtual concatenation beam edit can abort when a member cannot publish¶

    Concatenate two native images with tempclose=False. Remove table.lock from the second image and make its directory read-only while keeping the table files writable. CASA 6.7.6.14 reports success from setrestoringbeam, then aborts on done() when casacore cannot create table.dat_tmp. Casa-rs checks every native member's write access before the beam edit, so the call returns an error and the earlier member keeps its original beam. See #1625.

    A null field in saved image-expression metadata can crash image.open¶

    Create a saved Float expression with "MiscInfo": {"unknown": null} in its imageexpr.json and open the directory. CASA 6.7.6.14 can segfault while opening the manifest. Casa-rs rejects the null field with a catchable error. An absent MiscInfo field still inherits the operand record, and a present empty record still overrides it. See #1959.

    A relative saved-expression name can point at another directory after chdir¶

    Open a saved expression with a relative manifest path, then change the working directory. CASA 6.7.6.14 continues reading the original operands, but image.name() reports the manifest path relative to the new directory. Casa-rs records the manifest's absolute name at attachment so the name continues to identify the same image. See #1959.

    Cyclic saved expressions can crash image.open¶

    Create two saved image-expression directories whose ImageExpr fields refer to each other, then open either directory. CASA 6.7.6.14 recurses until the Python process segfaults. Casa-rs resolves aliases to the same directory and raises an error on the cycle before publishing an output. The same active path check covers a saved expression reached through a virtual concatenation. See #1959.

    Copying a saved expression can delete one of its manifests¶

    Use a native table directory as a saved expression by adding imageexpr.json, or put an expression directory inside a native table directory. Use that expression in an outer saved expression and copy the outer expression with fromimage or newimagefromimage, naming the native table as the destination and setting overwrite=True. CASA 6.7.6.14 succeeds and deletes the inner manifest, breaking the original outer expression. Casa-rs rejects an overwrite that overlaps any captured operand and preserves the receiver and source files. See #1959.

    Updating saved-expression metadata can overwrite another manifest¶

    Open expression.im by relative name, then change into a directory that also contains expression.im. CASA 6.7.6.14 writes setmiscinfo to the second directory while the tool still reads from the first expression. An external replacement at the original pathname can also receive the write. Casa-rs updates the original directory after a working-directory change. It refuses a stale write when the directory or manifest was replaced, even if the replacement contains the same expression. See #1959.

    Writing some saved-expression metadata can break reopen or lose values¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts NaN, infinity, empty arrays, and multidimensional arrays in setmiscinfo on an open saved image expression. Reopening can segfault for the non-finite values or reject the arrays. Casa-rs refuses these writes before changing the manifest or the live record. CASA can also omit a NumPy int64 scalar or truncate the elements of an int64 vector. Casa-rs stores wider integers without truncation in the same JSON fields, which both implementations can read. See #1959.

    Renaming a saved expression can move a replacement or erase an operand¶

    Open a named saved expression and move its directory outside the image tool. If another expression is then created at the old pathname, CASA 6.7.6.14 renames and opens the replacement. A relative name can also point at a different directory after chdir. Casa-rs preserves the captured directory and rejects an external replacement.

    Rename a saved expression with overwrite=True to the native table it reads, or to its own containing directory. CASA can replace the operand before segfaulting or delete the containing directory before reporting a move error. Casa-rs refuses overlapping destinations and moves that would remove a captured operand's pathname, including an alias stored inside the expression directory. This includes an alias reached through another alias to the expression directory. CASA can move the directory and then fail to reopen its operand, leaving the old pathname absent.

    If imageexpr.json links to ../manifest.json, moving the image under a different parent can make the link resolve to a different manifest. CASA accepts the move and attaches the replacement's metadata. Casa-rs preserves the referent and restores the original directory entries if the move would switch to a different manifest with the same expression. See #1959.

    Linked saved-expression writes can follow a changed referent¶

    Open a saved expression whose imageexpr.json is a symbolic link. Replacing that link or the file it points to after attachment makes CASA 6.7.6.14 write to the replacement on setmiscinfo, even when the live graph still uses the original expression. Casa-rs checks the captured link and file identities, rejects a stale update, and preserves the live metadata on failure. A successful update atomically replaces the file through its captured parent directory and leaves the link in place.

    On a move between two APFS filesystems, CASA copies the resolved file into a regular imageexpr.json. Casa-rs copies the link, verifies its referent at the final location, and keeps metadata writes directed to that referent. An internal relative link moves with its file. An external absolute link continues to share the existing file. See #1959.

    Uncached component-list images can count a point source twice¶

    Create a temporary component-list image of shape [6, 8] with a 2 Jy point source at the default direction reference and cache=False. In CASA 6.7.6.14, the first full read returns 2 Jy at [3, 4]. The next read returns 4 Jy there. The cached case returns 2 Jy on both reads. Casa-rs samples the same owned component model for each requested section and returns 2 Jy in either cache mode. See #1691.

    A scalar spectral index can give invalid polarized component-image pixels¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, create a point component with Stokes flux [2, 1, 0, 0] Jy, reference frequency 1.415 GHz and scalar spectral index -3. Sample a component image with Stokes I and Q and frequencies 1 kHz to either side of the reference. The Q values can depend on other allocations in the Python process. SpectralIndex::sampleStokes indexes four parameters in its matrix overload when the scalar input supplied one. The explicit vector [-3, 0, 0, 0] produces the expected power law in both planes. Casa-rs returns that same power law for the scalar form. See #1691.

    A renamed component-image mask can retain its previous table path¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, create a native component-list image with a mask, copy the mask, select the copy as the default and rename it. maskhandler("default") returns the new name, but reading the mask through that attachment can fail with a file error for the old directory. Reopening the image reads the renamed table. Casa-rs in the same attachment reads the mask from its new path when the rename succeeds. See #1691.

    An attached virtual concatenation can write to a retargeted input symlink¶

    Create a nomove concatenation using a symlink as one input, then retarget that symlink to a second image of the same shape while the tool is still attached. CASA 6.7.6.14 reads the new image and sends putchunk writes to it under both TempClose settings. casa-rs pins the physical input for the attachment, so the write reaches the original image. A new open resolves the manifest paths again. This prevents an existing handle from modifying an unrelated image.

    See #1749.

    A strided write to a virtual concatenation can abort at a skipped member¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, concatenate three [3, 4] Float members along axis zero with mode="nomove" and relax=True, with the first member repeated in the third position. A [2, 1] write from blc=[0, 0] with inc=[6, 1] aborts Python. The middle member intersects the bounding interval but has no selected samples. Casa-rs skips members with no requested samples and writes the two samples in order to the single physical member. See #1749.

    Failed virtual concatenation can leave inputs and a previous output displaced¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, concatenate images with shapes [2, 3] and [2, 4] along axis zero. With mode="copy" the shape error leaves partial copies in the output. With mode="move" the error can leave both operands in that directory, with the original paths gone. A pre-existing destination can be removed before validation. casa-rs checks shape and path constraints first, publishes the complete output, and restores original names if a later step fails. Same-filesystem moves and rollback rename entries without duplicating pixel data. Across filesystems the move makes the necessary destination copy once and holds the original until publication succeeds.

    Distinct operands from different directories can also have the same basename. CASA's copy can replace the first copy and bind both sections to the second operand. Move can remove both originals and retain only the second. casa-rs refuses the conflict before transferring either image.

    An input can itself be a virtual image whose manifest refers to sibling images. Copying or moving it together with other images of those same basenames can silently substitute the other images in the nested product. casa-rs checks the manifest graph and symbolic links in the proposed directory layout before transferring the inputs. A chain of relative symlinks can move together when it continues to resolve to the same image.

    With a saved expression and its referenced native image as operands, mode="move" can displace both inputs and leave a product whose expression still points to the old pathname. Using the expression's referenced table as the output can also crash Python in mode="nomove". Casa-rs checks the transitive operands and the proposed storage layout before publication. See #1625.

    See #1749.

    Renaming a sibling-relative virtual image can displace a readable image¶

    Create a nomove concatenation of two sibling images in CASA 6.7.6.14 and rename it into a new parent directory. The operands remain in the old parent, so reopen fails after CASA moves the virtual directory. casa-rs checks operand resolution before rename and refuses a destination that changes the bindings, including an owned member linked to an external relative target. Renaming a self-contained tree preserves its nested member paths across parent directories.

    See #1749.

    calcmask can crash on decisive Boolean validity¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, create source.im as a float image with values [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and default mask "source.im" > 2. On another image of shape [2, 2], calcmask('mask(("source.im" > 0) || T)') and calcmask('mask(("source.im" > 0) && F)') terminate Python with SIGSEGV. Reversing the operands also crashes. An unmasked image predicate can trigger the same failure, for example mask(("source.im" > 2) || (value("source.im") <= 2)).

    casa-rs evaluates validity per pixel. A known true operand makes OR valid, and a known false operand makes AND valid. Where neither operand determines the result, both operands must be valid. The resulting validity mask is all true in these reproductions. #1625

    calc can crash on a mixed-precision vector¶

    With a temporary float image of shape [3], CASA 6.7.6.14 terminates Python with SIGSEGV when evaluating calc("[1, 2.5, 4] + 1", False) or calc("[-1.25, -2e1, +3.2]", False). The inputs mix single and double precision scalars in an array literal.

    casa-rs promotes those elements using the expression's numeric types and stores the results [2, 3.5, 5] and [-1.25, -20, 3.2] as float pixels. #1625

    imagecalc can publish pixels before rejecting the metadata source¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, evaluate imagecalc('out.im', '"source.im" * 3', True, 'missing.im') with a valid float source.im and a missing metadata image. CASA raises RuntimeError after writing the calculated pixels to out.im. If out.im already held an unrelated image, the same failed call replaces its original pixels.

    casa-rs validates the metadata source and stages the product before publication. The failed call preserves an existing output and leaves a new output path absent. #1625

    The same staging protects inputs of a saved metadata expression. For out.im containing leaf.im, use a saved imagemd expression that reads out.im/leaf.im and request imagecalc(..., outfile='out.im', overwrite=True). CASA deletes the nested input before failing to open the metadata. Casa-rs rejects the overlap and keeps both tables. An exact reference to out.im is valid and reads the new staged output.

    An analysis output can remove an entry needed by its mask expression¶

    Use a saved expression as the mask operand of subimage and replace an existing native out.im. In CASA 6.7.6.14, the replacement can delete a symbolic link inside out.im used to reach the saved image or one of its leaves. It can also delete the referent of a linked imageexpr.json inside out.im. A leaf read can then fail after the original directory is gone. Casa-rs checks the entries used by the mask before publication and keeps the original table. A disjoint sibling reached through the same directory link is still writable. See #1627.

    A saved imagecalc operand can return a stale cached section¶

    With imagecalc(pixels='"expr.im" + 1'), where the saved expr.im contains "leaf.im" * 3, read a one-pixel section, unlock the result, and add 50 to the underlying leaf.im with another tool. CASA 6.7.6.14 can return its previous value on the next read of the same section. Casa-rs returns the updated value on that read. See #1625.

    imagecalc can read a different FITS operand after a directory change¶

    Create two directories with an input.fits of the same shape in each. Give the first image pixel value 2 and the second image pixel value 21. In the first directory, create a lazy CASA 6.7.6.14 result using imagecalc(pixels='"input.fits" * 3'). Change to the second directory before the first pixel read. CASA returns 63 while keeping the first file's metadata. With a native image operand, CASA returns 6 in this sequence.

    casa-rs resolves the operand paths when creating the result and returns 6 with the original FITS metadata. The FITS handle is opened on the first pixel read and retained for subsequent reads. #1625

    image.addnoise can erase pixels or fail to return on unusable input¶

    Fill an image with nonzero pixels and call ia.addnoise("normal", [0, -1], zero=True, seeds=[1, 2]). CASA 6.7.6.14 zeros the region before reporting an illegal variance. An unknown distribution such as "bogus" has the same destructive order. casa-rs validates the distribution before writing the existing image. Passing seeds=None explicitly can also change the image before the Python wrapper raises SystemError. casa-rs rejects that argument before changing pixels.

    CASA also fails to return for a one-pixel image with ia.addnoise("geometric", [0], seeds=[1, 2]) or ia.addnoise("poisson", [800], seeds=[1, 2]). The geometric rejection loop cannot draw a uniform zero with those seeds. The Poisson bound underflows to zero, leaving its product loop true after the product reaches zero. casa-rs returns a Python error for these inputs.

    PlotMS leaves calibration-table header values blank¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 with casaplotms 2.9.1 exports labels such as File: and Observation date: when headeritems is set on a current bandpass table. The corresponding values are blank even in a wide export with only headeritems='filename'. Casa-rs reads available values from the table and lays them out within the requested figure dimensions. Wildcard row IDs leave the matching metadata values blank. Calibration diagnostics #1526

    PlotMS can fail when a calibration-table transform is enabled¶

    With CASA 6.7.6.14 and casaplotms 2.9.1, enabling freqframe='BARY' or freqframe='TOPO' on the same bandpass table failed in the headless plotting process before completing the export. CalCache::loadIt documents the calibration-table behavior with its warning that transformations are ignored. Casa-rs emits that warning and exports the stored spectral coordinates. Both engines produced identical text when transform=False with nondefault frame, rest frequency and velocity convention. Calibration diagnostics #1526

    Mixed averaged flagdata can leave row flags clear¶

    On the public Four_ants_3C286.ms fixture, CASA 6.7.6.14's stock mixed Clip, TFCrop, RFlag, and antint list test starts from cleared flags. The shared iterator averages pairs of integrations and groups channels in bins of eight. The task flags 591,808 samples and leaves FLAG_ROW false for 26 of the 486 rows whose samples are all flagged in the repeated stock replay. The same 26 rows occur with the Clip, TFCrop, and RFlag prefix alone. An interleaved timing replay returned another row mask with identical sample flags. CASA's AveragingTvi2::writeFlag derives the row flag from the propagated sample mask. Casa-rs preserves that rule after projecting the final shared mask to the input rows. The stock test passes and every sample flag agrees with CASA.

    Calibration quack can flag the whole scan when times are out of order¶

    With CASA 6.7.6.14, two Tsys time blocks in the same scan stored in reverse order are both flagged by quackinterval=1.0 with either quackmode='beg' or quackmode='endb', even though their timestamps are ten seconds apart. The calibration handler uses the first and last eligible stored rows to derive the scan boundaries. Casa-rs uses the eligible timestamps and flags the chronological beginning or end as requested.

    Calibration flagdata ignores a channel stride¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 manually flags channels 1 through 5 on current CPARAM bandpass and FPARAM Tsys tables for spw='0:1~5^2'. The channel stride selects channels 1, 3, and 5. Casa-rs flags those channels and preserves channels 2 and 4. The calibration flagdata oracle checks both outcomes.

    Calibration RFlag can extend flags outside the selected channels¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, flagdata(mode='rflag', spw='0:3~7') with automatic extension can flag channel 0 in both CPARAM bandpass and FPARAM Tsys tables. The corresponding selected channels agree with casa-rs, which preserves every flag outside the requested slice on both calibration tables and MeasurementSets.

    On a calibration table or MeasurementSet, winsize=0 and winsize=-1 abort the CASA process with an out-of-range vector access. Casa-rs rejects nonpositive window lengths before running the agent.

    Using a positive explicit time or frequency threshold with a zero or negative scale can also crash CASA while applying flags on either a calibration table or a MeasurementSet. Casa-rs rejects these combinations before writing flags. Calculate mode ignores the scale factors and reports the unscaled calculated thresholds.

    Calibration flagdata summary can crash on a wildcard field¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 flagdata(mode='summary') can segfault on a delay table created by gencal(caltype='sbd'), whose FIELD_ID is -1. Casa-rs counts the flags and uses the literal -1 key for the wildcard field. The calibration flagdata oracle runs the CASA call in a separate process and verifies the native report and unchanged input.

    Calibration command lists can abort or flag beyond an unmatched selector¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 aborts with a vector allocation error when an antenna integration command names the physical CPARAM or FPARAM column in a calibration flag list. Casa-rs raises a ValueError identifying the required visibility input and preserves the table's flags. The single-task mode='antint' call on these tables raises CASA's agent-configuration error.

    In a multi-command list, an antenna or field name that matches no calibration rows can cause CASA to flag the whole table. Casa-rs rejects the selector before publishing staged edits. The calibration command-list oracle verifies both the unmatched-antenna refusal and the antenna-integration crash case.

    On an FPARAM table, a local antenna='!A1' spw='0:1' command followed by a summary can flag only A1. Used alone, the same command can leave all flags unchanged. Casa-rs flags the selected channel for antennas other than A1 in both cases. The oracle checks each mask against the original table.

    The direct agentflagger tool can abort when its antenna-integration agent names a physical CPARAM or FPARAM column. In casa-rs, run() raises a RuntimeError and leaves the stored flags intact, including when an earlier agent staged a flag edit. An unmatched local antenna selector also raises before publication. The direct calibration agent oracle checks both paths and verifies that the next run starts without the consumed agents.

    With a direct manual calibration agent configured with array='9' and antenna='A2', CASA cancels filtering and flags every antenna. Casa-rs keeps the valid antenna restriction to avoid changing flags on unrelated rows. The direct oracle checks both masks on CPARAM and FPARAM tables.

    PlotMS shows the excluded antenna on a GSPLINE plot¶

    On a GSPLINE table with antennas A0 through A4, CASA 6.7.6.14 and casaplotms 2.9.1 plot only A2 for antenna="!A2". The legacy selector excludes A2 from the source row query, then passes the excluded ID to the plot cache as an antenna to display. The cache evaluates and plots that ID. casa-rs applies the exclusion to the source rows and plots A0, A1, A3, and A4. The legacy calibration PlotMS oracle checks both outcomes.

    PlotMS averages disjoint channel selections on a compressed sample grid¶

    With CASA 6.7.6.14, a callibrary, spw='0:0~2;5~7' and avgchannel='2', PlotMS retains frequency bins for original channels 0–1 and 5–6. It averages visibility samples from original channels 0–1 and 2 and 5, in the order of its compressed channel buffer. casa-rs preserves the paired text coordinates and sample values so existing PlotMS diagnostics can be compared directly (#1526).

    impv can lose overlap on small rotated strips¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, a 12-by-12 direction plane can report that the input and rotated output do not overlap even when both endpoints are at least two pixels from the edges. Examples are a reversed horizontal cut from [8,6] to [3,6] and a vertical cut from [5,3] to [5,8]. Padding the input direction plane before the same sky-coordinate cut restores the CASA result. casa-rs interpolates only the requested strip and agrees with the padded CASA reference without requiring callers to pad the input (#1024).

    impv masks early validation errors during cleanup¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 raises UnboundLocalError when outfile is empty, when coordinate mode lacks an endpoint, or when length mode lacks a center, length, or position angle. The task raises its validation error before assigning myia, then the finally block references that local. casa-rs identifies the missing parameter or mode-specific selection and leaves no output. The upstream suite checks each implementation's error (#977).

    imregrid drops brightness units and the beam when broadcasting a channel¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, imregrid with a one-channel input, an explicitly selected spectral axis and a multi-channel output replicates the data and mask. During that copy it loses the brightness unit and restoring beam. The singleton case in crates/casa-images/tests/data/imregrid/expected.json records a Jy/beam image with a 4 by 3 arcsec beam becoming a unitless image without a beam. casa-rs matches the samples, mask and template frequency grid and retains the original units and beam. Copying channels does not change the calibration of the pixels being copied.

    imregrid can terminate when shifting a sliced direction¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 on macOS returns the original pixels and mask when regridding the unchanged direction axis of the 3 × 2 × 5 dropdeg_ra.image fixture. Increasing the retained axis's reference pixel by 0.25 in the same template record makes the task terminate with SIGBUS. The casacore regrid path treats a direction coordinate as a two-axis plane even when an axis has been removed. Casa-rs preserves the unchanged slice directly. It refused the shifted fixture with an all-masked result and published no output.

    imregrid can attach new linear coordinates to unshifted data¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 can copy pixels and masks unchanged when regridding a leading axis of a three-axis linear coordinate at the same shape. The same_shape_linear_shift case in crates/casa-images/tests/data/imregrid/expected.json changes the first axis's reference value by 0.25 m on a 7 × 6 × 5 image. CASA reports the new reference value but retains the source samples. In casacore's LinearCoordinate::near, the exclusion loop marks consecutive entries instead of the indexes in the supplied exclusion list. The comparison can therefore skip the axis being regridded.

    Casa-rs samples the shifted grid and updates the mask. For unit-spaced pixels, the first two samples with values 0 and 1 yield 0.25 at output pixel zero. The last sample lies outside the input and is masked. The fixture records both CASA's actual product and the independently calculated shift.

    Legacy MosaicFT rejects split voltage-pattern image records¶

    The CASA 6.7.6.14 legacy HetArrayConvFunc::findAntennaSizes checks for realimage and imagimage in a custom IMAGE record. It reads the imaginary image from imagim. vpmanager.setpbimage saves the standard field imagimage. The public imager.ft then reports that imagim is unknown and returns false.

    The same responses packaged as complex Jones images work through the public legacy imager. Adding imagim as an alias in the split records also works and gives the same CASA prediction. casa-rs reads the standard field for native prediction. For virtual interoperation, the Fourier grid owns a copy of the voltage-pattern table with the alias. A real-only pattern uses a zero-valued imaginary image owned by the same grid. Calibration model outcome · imager_custom_mosaic_oracle.py

    Image collapse can abort or shift a wrapped longitude by 180 degrees¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 aborts for negative or duplicate axes, for example ia.collapse("sum", [-1]) and ia.collapse("sum", [0, 0]). casa-rs raises a Python error before replacing the output.
