    On a default 4 × 4 direction image, ia.collapse("sum", [0, 1]) also averages longitudes on opposite sides of the 0-degree meridian as ordinary numbers. CASA reports a longitude near 180 degrees for a footprint centered about half an arcminute from the meridian. casa-rs unwraps both endpoints around the interior sky position before averaging, so the result remains on the selected footprint. This also keeps the midpoint on fields broader than 180 degrees.

    CASA 6.7.6.14 also segfaults collapsing a Stokes–Frequency image whose native record puts Frequency at pixel axis 1 and world axis 0. casa-rs resolves axes="Frequency" through the native world-to-pixel map and collapses the corresponding pixel axis.

    Continuum subtraction leaves a partial product for aliased outputs¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts the same initially absent path for outline and outcont in image.continuumsub. It writes the continuum model before raising an error while publishing the residual. With overwrite enabled, CASA still reports an error after writing the model. casa-rs rejects aliased destinations before fitting and verifies both destinations before publishing either image.

    A zero-stride region aborts image.modify¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 terminates with SIGABRT and an uncaught casacore::ArraySlicerError when image.modify uses an LCSlicer record whose increment is zero. A scratch probe used a 7 × 7 float image and a point component, with the first increment of a region covering [1, 1] through [5, 5] set to zero. Casa-rs raises a Python error during region validation and preserves the stored pixels and history (#1625). The same zero-stride record also aborts CASA when passed to ia.fromimage or ia.newimagefromimage. Casa-rs reports a Python error before copying.

    Legacy imager single-dish Gaussian settings and virtual recipes¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 constructs the default single-dish imager with an empty convertfirst string. An explicit setsdoptions(convertfirst='NEVER') allows imager.ft to proceed. casa-rs starts with that default.

    The legacy SDGrid copy constructor omits the Gaussian widths and cutoff that CubeSkyEquation needs when it initializes the live model. On a smooth ALMA model with off-centre recorded pointings, pinned SF and BOX produce nonzero scratch models. The pinned GAUSS control returns zero even with an explicit positive cutoff. casa-rs evaluates GAUSS and GJINC from their kernel equations. The paired oracle uses the pinned pointing coordinates and independent Gaussian and Bessel evaluations.

    CASA publishes an SDGrid record for sd without the kernel settings. For both, GridBoth::toRecord writes its two transforms into the same record, leaving the SDGrid name and image with some GridFT fields. Pinned uvsub rejects the records for both modes. casa-rs saves the single-dish settings with the complex SDGrid image and gives GridFT its own entry for both. The CASA image tool opens both backing images, and native uvsub reopens the models. An incomplete CASA recipe raises an error that identifies the missing settings.

    Standalone SDGrid uses the interpolator selected by freqinterp for scratch prediction. Its native saved recipe retains that choice and the original channel span on reopen, including the single-channel bypass. GridBoth delegates prediction to its two child transforms. The legacy frequency setter updates the parent, so both children use nearest neighbour. In the pinned five-plane test, all four methods produce identical mixed-grid outputs. The native mixed-grid prediction follows that behavior.

    With setvp(dovp=True), pinned scratch prediction applies the field's sky voltage pattern as it advances through the visibility buffers. Its virtual recipe stores the first apparent sky for the selected fields. The beam oracle compares the stored sky pixels with CASA, then uses that pinned image as input to a separate CASA scratch prediction to verify native readback. Standalone SDGrid takes custom gridding beams. GridBoth keeps its default gridding beam and can still apply a custom sky voltage pattern. The legacy voltage-pattern lookup uses the first concrete table row for the telescope. A later row marked as the VPManager default does not change that choice.

    SDGrid can include a cross-correlation when all of its UVW components are nonpositive. casa-rs applies the single-dish contribution to autocorrelations. In both, the ordinary GridFT path predicts the cross-correlations.

    For fast scans, CASA normally fits a natural cubic through each antenna's pointings. Its linear fallback can take neighboring rows from another antenna when the short sequence is interleaved. casa-rs interpolates over the recorded samples of the requested antenna. With an empty POINTING table, casa-rs applies the first feed's offset to the field direction. The paired test uses pinned measures to shift the field in its reference. The pinned SDGrid copy also drops the requested conversion order and disables the pointing cache. casa-rs retains both controls. In the conversion-order test, pinned CASA measures convert each AZEL control point at its recorded epoch. A second pinned run samples that converted track in the image frame. Calibration model outcome · imager_single_dish_oracle.py · imager_single_dish_options_oracle.py · imager_single_dish_spectral_oracle.py · imager_single_dish_beam_oracle.py

    Legacy pbwproject virtual recipes lack a machine name¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 predicts nonzero complex model visibilities in the legacy VLA single-W-plane case with a new or existing convolution cache. nPBWProjectFT::toRecord saves an image and transform geometry. It omits the Fourier-machine name and the convolution needed to repeat the prediction. Pinned ms.uvsub refuses that record with field name is unknown. Its virtual-model reader also lacks an nPBWProjectFT constructor.

    Casa-rs shares the cache generator with the legacy EP workflow and retains the Fourier image and its convolution in a native recipe. The CASA image tool opens both images. Native ms.uvsub reopens the model after the original cache is removed from its path. Both readers refuse the incomplete pinned recipe before subtracting a visibility model. imager_legacy_pbw_oracle.py · Calibration model outcome

    FITS export can change axis lengths or abort while removing axes¶

    With CASA 6.7.6.14, export a float image of shape [3, 4, 2, 1] with a two-plane Stokes axis and one spectral channel using image.tofits with deglast=True and stokeslast=True. The output declares two spectral channels and two Stokes planes even though the source has only 24 pixels. The degenerate-axis pass uses the input extents after the Stokes pass has already changed their order. casa-rs writes [3, 4, 1, 2] and preserves all pixel values and their coordinates.

    CASA also raises Unknown error copying image to FITS file when moving a leading singleton axis in a linear image of shape [1, 4, 2] with deglast=True. casa-rs writes [4, 2, 1] with the data in the matching axis order, readable in CASA.

    On the pinned Linux build, dropdeg=True on a [1, 1, 1, 1] float image can terminate Python with SIGFPE. casa-rs raises RuntimeError because no image axes would remain. See #1625.

    Image region collapse can select the first pixel or abort¶

    With a 5×4×2 image whose coordinate is linear, CASA 6.7.6.14 image.getregion(axes=[0]) can return shape (1, 1, 2) with the first two input pixels. With the standard coordinates and double-complex pixels, the same call can terminate the process.

    casa-rs averages valid pixels over the requested axes and retains all other axes, for every supported image pixel type (#1627).

    Empty integer selectors can abort MeasurementSet metadata queries¶

    On an attached msmetadata tool, CASA 6.7.6.14 aborts the process when namesforfields, namesforspws, bandwidths, rxbands, or subwindows receives a zero-length NumPy integer array, such as numpy.array([], dtype=numpy.int64). Its integer-vector path computes a minimum on the empty array and the resulting casacore exception escapes the Python binding. An empty Python list selects all values through the default path.

    casa-rs treats an empty integer array as an empty selector and returns the same result as the corresponding omitted argument (#1029).

    Explicit observation and array IDs can select an uninitialized scan key¶

    On an attached CASA 6.7.6.14 msmetadata tool, get a valid scan number from scannumbers(0, 0) and call fieldsforscans([scan], obsid=0, arrayid=0) or timesforscans([scan], obsid=0, arrayid=0). The vector selection initializes the scan number but leaves the observation and array IDs uninitialized. CASA can report an unknown scan with unrelated IDs. The single-scan and asmap=True variants do use the supplied IDs.

    casa-rs uses the requested observation, array, and scan number for the vector selection too, and reports an error for a missing scan (#1029).

    Scan queries can abort on an empty MeasurementSet¶

    Create a valid MeasurementSet with no MAIN rows and open it with msmetadata. In CASA 6.7.6.14, calling narrays() or scannumbers() then terminates the process with an uncaught casacore exception. The array-ID check calls max on the empty MAIN column.

    casa-rs reports zero arrays and returns an empty scan-number array (numpy.int64) for the default query, consistent with nscans() returning zero on the same MeasurementSet (#1029).

    Unsupported scan-selector array types can select every scan¶

    With CASA 6.7.6.14, pass a nonempty numpy.float16 or object array to msmetadata.fieldsforscans. CASA emits a conversion message, discards the supplied scan numbers, and returns fields for every scan. casa-rs raises TypeError so the unsupported array type cannot silently widen the selection (#1029).

    Field time selection can include the first field after the time window¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, open a MeasurementSet whose first MAIN time is after zero and call msmetadata.fieldsfortimes(0.0, 0.0). The result includes the first observed field because the loop collects fields before testing the upper bound. casa-rs includes only fields with an observation time inside the requested inclusive interval (#1029).

    Empty or out-of-range time selectors can terminate CASA¶

    For an attached CASA 6.7.6.14 msmetadata tool, passing numpy.array([], dtype=numpy.int64) to timesforscans can segfault because the binding dereferences the minimum of an empty vector. Passing the same array to timesforspws can abort with an empty-array exception. In timesforspws, a positive scalar outside the spectral window table can also segfault because that path indexes without a bounds check.

    casa-rs interprets the empty integer vector as the full in-scope set and raises RuntimeError for the out-of-range spectral window (#1029).

    An unsigned scalar can widen a spectral-window time selection¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, open a MeasurementSet with more than one spectral window. msmetadata.timesforspws(numpy.uint32(0)) returns a dictionary covering all windows. A Python integer, signed NumPy integer, or one-element unsigned integer array returns the requested window. casa-rs treats the unsigned scalar as the requested window too, so its numeric value cannot be lost and the selection widened (#1029).

    Image coordinate frequency conversion can use the wrong physical direction¶

    Create a CASA 6.7.6.14 image with shape [20,20,20] and the default J2000 direction (0,0) at the reference pixel. Set the direction conversion to B1950 and the spectral conversion to CMB. The converted direction coordinates then enter the frequency measures frame labeled as J2000. The returned frequency is wrong regardless of the direction reporting frame requested by the caller.

    For the reference pixel's LSRK frequency of 1.415 GHz, the pinned image.coordmeasures tool returns approximately 1,416,700,650.518 Hz in CMB, 1,414,142,155.337 Hz in LGROUP and 1,415,002,053.555 Hz in BARY. CASA's independent measures tool reproduces these results when fed the mislabeled coordinates. Both casa-rs and the independent conversion with the actual J2000 direction agree within 0.001 Hz on 1,416,697,167.835 Hz, 1,414,138,758.484 Hz and 1,415,001,368.979 Hz respectively. The native frequency context uses the physical position, independently of the direction chosen for the returned record.

    The 45-degree image rotation fixture assumes prior floating-point rounding¶

    The CASA 6.7.6.14 upstream ia_rotate_test.test_basic rotates prerot.im by 45 degrees and compares every pixel with the archived postrot.im. It requires a maximum absolute difference below 1e-21. Pinned CASA reproduced the archive within 4.24e-22 on the validation host.

    Both backends preserve the float32 image pixel type, 200-by-200 shape, float64 Python chunk dtype, and exact 33,272-pixel validity mask. On valid pixels, casa-rs differs from the archive by 9.52e-9 normalized RMS and at most 5.96e-8. The largest difference is between adjacent float32 values near 0.64. Returning those values in a float64 array does not increase the accuracy of the stored pixels. The companion test checks the image types, dimensions, mask, and numerical agreement at float32 precision. The upstream assertion remains unchanged.

    Image statistics can report an extremum outside the sampled pixels¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, ia.statistics(region=...) on a box starting at [1, 1, 0] with stride [2, 1, 1] can report maxpos=[2, 2, 1] for the maximum at image pixel [3, 2, 1]. The first coordinate omits the region's sampling stride, so the reported position was never selected. casa-rs maps extrema to absolute image pixels using the original stride. The same reporting issue affects the plane indices written to a statistics logfile. With a channel selection of 1, 3, 5, CASA prints 1, 2, 3. casa-rs reports the actual selected channel indices next to their world values.

    An unfiltered ia.statistics() on a 5×4×2 image created with linear=True and pixel values 0 through 39 reports npts=2 and sum=1, even though ia.getchunk() reads the full image. Casa-rs measures all 40 pixels and reports sum=780 and trc=[4, 3, 1].

    On a three-axis image, ia.statistics(axes=[0, 0]) can also terminate the process. casa-rs raises an error for the duplicate axis.

    The pinned biweight algorithm can also terminate when every selected pixel is masked. casa-rs returns a recoverable error for the empty sample.

    Image statistics can fail after dropping one direction axis¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, create a Float image with shape [9, 1, 1, 5], fill it with x + 10 * channel, and call subimage(dropdeg=True) to retain one direction axis and the frequency axis. statistics on an LCSlicer from [1, 1] through [7, 4] with stride [2, 2] raises a WCSLIB wcsp2s error while formatting the selected coordinates. The same region is readable with getregion. Casa-rs returns the pixel statistics, including the analytic sample count of 8 and sum of 192.

    Image statistics can use the wrong beam for a selected channel¶

    On a direction, Stokes and spectral cube with distinct beams for I and Q, select one channel and compute ia.statistics(axes=[0, 1], region=...). CASA 6.7.6.14 can divide both polarization sums by the beam area for I. The selected channel is degenerate, and the beam lookup assigns the polarization index to the channel dimension. casa-rs maps each result to its original channel and Stokes beam.

    Image statistics can remove channels when selecting polarizations¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, call statistics(axes=[0, 1], region=...) on a [3, 4, 8, 4] direction, spectral and Stokes image. Select all eight channels and only Stokes I and V with regionmanager.frombcs. CASA returns arrays of shape (6, 4) because it removes channel planes 1 and 2 while leaving the excluded polarizations in the result. Casa-rs returns shape (8, 2) with the eight original channels and only I and V. It applies each region exclusion to the corresponding display axis.

    Setting the pixels of a complex image can terminate CASA¶

    On the pinned Linux build of CASA 6.7.6.14, image.fromshape(shape=[3, 4], type="c") followed by image.set(pixels=2) terminates Python with SIGSEGV. casa-rs raises RuntimeError and preserves the complex image. See #1625.

    Legacy AW prediction needs a usable sensitivity image for PB correction¶

    With CASA 6.7.6.14, the legacy imager.ft routes awproject and mawproject predict the same visibilities on the original VLA fixture. A tclean CFS cache works directly when dopbgriddingcorrections=False. With correction enabled, the legacy imager fails in its sensitivity-image lattice setup if the cache contains no avgPB. Supplying an avgPB image with the model's axes permits the corrected prediction. The cold legacy run on the same fixture fails while setting up its convolution cells.

    The legacy writer emits the model image and the AWProjectWBFT name but omits its convolution cache. Its own ms.uvsub reports Unsupported FTMachine. Casa-rs retains the kernel images with the model. CASA can open the backing images, and native ms.uvsub uses them after the source cache has moved. The native reader reports an error if the saved recipe has no retained kernel images. imager_legacy_aw_oracle.py · Calibration model outcome

    Legacy A/W can read beyond its channel-to-kernel map¶

    With wideband legacy awproject or mawproject in CASA 6.7.6.14, selectvis(spw='0:0;3') spans four visibility channels. CFBuffer::initMaps overwrites each spectral window's map with the last range's entries. Here the last range defines one entry. AWVisResampler::GridToData indexes the map with the compact visibility channel number, leaving indices beyond the first entry without a defined kernel selection.

    Casa-rs follows the last range for indices within the map and looks up the cell nearest the physical channel frequency for later indices. Perturbing the two cache frequencies independently confirms that both engines use the last range's kernel at index zero in either range order. imager_legacy_aw_oracle.py

    image.insert aborts for a source that misses along one axis¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 terminates with SIGABRT and Slicer error:end<start for a [2, 2] source inserted into a [4, 4] target at locate=[10, 1] or [-10, 1]. One axis overlaps. The other yields an empty clipped interval. The casa-rs tool raises a Python RuntimeError before writing pixels or mask bits.

    image.insert can replace unread source pixels during a self-insert¶

    Create a native float image from a 1510 by 1510 ramp in NumPy row order and insert the source region box([0, 0], [1508, 1508]) into the same image at locate=[1, 1]. CASA 6.7.6.14 returns success and persists 27,063 wrong pixels. For example, (2, 152) contains 150 instead of the original value 1661 from (1, 151). The cursor writes overlap pixels that a subsequent cursor reads. casa-rs snapshots the selected pixels and validity before writing, using scratch storage when the overlap exceeds its memory budget.

    A non-finite scalar coordinate order can terminate CASA¶

    Create a one-axis Linear coordinate system and pass a bare float("inf") to transpose or reorder. Both calls terminate the CASA 6.7.6.14 process on macOS arm64. With [float("inf")], CASA raises its ordinary axis error. Casa-rs applies the arm64 axis conversion to either form and rejects the axis with an ordinary Python exception, preserving the coordinate system. See #1626.

    coordsys.setrestfrequency can store an infinite frequency¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts cs.setrestfrequency(float('inf')) and writes an infinite active rest frequency. That value cannot produce meaningful Doppler velocities. casa-rs raises RuntimeError and retains the previous frequency list, active frequency and coordinate transform.

    coordsys.setrestfrequency can crash on a whitespace-only string¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 terminates with SIGSEGV when cs.setrestfrequency(' ') tokenizes the string and tries to read the first quantity from an empty list. casa-rs raises RuntimeError and retains the existing list.

    coordsys.setreferencelocation can crash when an axis is masked¶

    On a two-axis linear coordinate, CASA 6.7.6.14 terminates with SIGSEGV for cs.setreferencelocation([2, 3], [8.0, 9.0], [True, False]). The same failure can occur with a Stokes axis because the method excludes Stokes from the edit. casa-rs changes both reference values on each enabled non-Stokes axis and preserves both values on the other axes. It publishes the updated coordinate state only after the complete edit succeeds.

    imager.ft can crash after a refused duplicate image with a new component¶

    With the same live CASA 6.7.6.14 imager, predict an image, then submit that image again together with an unused component list. ft reports a duplicate image. A subsequent call with just the component reports that the component is already present, and a no-input ft() can terminate with SIGSEGV. casa-rs refuses the mixed duplicate request before adding the component. The same imager can repeat the original image prediction and can subsequently add the component alone.

    Coordsys relative conversions can abort on missing values¶

    On a two-axis coordinate system, CASA 6.7.6.14 aborts for cs.toabs(isworld=0) and cs.toabs(isworld=1). casa-rs interprets the omitted values as zero offsets and returns the reference position in the requested domain. CASA also aborts when toabsmany or torelmany receives a matrix with fewer rows than the number of coordinate axes. casa-rs raises RuntimeError for these matrices.

    Coordsys spectral velocity conversions can crash on missing input¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, calling frequencytovelocity or velocitytofrequency with an empty vector on a spectral coordinate exits with SIGSEGV. Calling velocitytofrequency([1.0]) without a spectral coordinate also exits with SIGSEGV when it looks up the default frequency unit. casa-rs returns an empty float64 array for empty vectors on a spectral coordinate and raises RuntimeError when the spectral coordinate is missing.

    Coordsys Doppler conversion can misread byte-swapped arrays¶

    On a little-endian host, CASA 6.7.6.14 treats a big-endian float64 NumPy array such as np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], dtype='>f8') as native-endian bytes in frequencytofrequency. The values become tiny subnormal numbers even at zero velocity. casa-rs respects the array dtype's byte order.

    Coordsys linear transform input can abort or make a record unreadable¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 can abort in setlineartransform('linear', value) on a three-dimensional numeric array. It can also accept a zero transform for a sampled tabular or spectral coordinate, then write constant lookup values that its record reader refuses to reopen. casa-rs raises RuntimeError before editing the coordinate in these cases. It also rejects non-finite matrix coefficients and reads byte-swapped arrays according to their declared byte order.

    Coordsys tabular samples can leave an unreadable coordinate¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts settabular([0, 0, 2], [5, 6, 7]) and then raises Interpolate1D::operator() data has repeated x values in torecord(). The interpolator also treats adjacent pixels within 1e-13 as repeated. It also accepts nonfinite samples, which can turn even finite input positions into NaN. casa-rs rejects these samples before changing the coordinate. Finite one-sample tables still define constant mappings.

    CASA also replaces the samples when either argument is a tuple, then raises a Python SystemError after the replacement. casa-rs raises the Python error before changing the coordinate.

    image.statistics can overwrite a logfile omitted from the current call¶

    With CASA 6.7.6.14, call ia.statistics(logfile='report.txt'), replace the file contents, then call ia.statistics(append=False) on the same image tool. The second call truncates the previously selected file even though logfile was omitted. casa-rs uses a logfile only on calls that explicitly supply its path.

    image.rebin can raise after writing an output with tuple factors¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 writes the named output of ia.rebin("output.im", (2, 2)) and then raises a Python SystemError. A list with the same values succeeds. casa-rs reads the factors as integers and returns the rebinned image for either sequence.

    Coordinate setters and measure input with a removed world axis¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts a two-axis linear coordinate record with worldmap0=[-1,0] and both pixel axes retained. Its reference measure correctly retains both local quantities. Passing that measure to coordsys.topixel aborts the process. Giving the same record to coordsys.setreferencevalue with type="linear" also aborts when the tool addresses the removed world slot. The typed setter can abort for a direction coordinate with the same map.

    casa-rs decodes the complete measure and uses the coordinate record's replacement when conversion needs the hidden world component. A typed numeric edit accepts the visible components in local order or the full local vector. Edits from either representation update visible axes and retain the hidden value and its replacement. The mapped inspection and conversion tests exercise these cases. See #1002 and #1819.

    Typed coordinate units with different pixel and world orders¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 indexes the world-unit vector with pixel positions in coordsys.units(type=...). In a record whose direction pixel axes are [1,0] and world axes are [0,2], CASA reports direction units ["","rad"] and Stokes units ["rad"]. The empty unit belongs to Stokes. casa-rs uses the coordinate's world axes and reports ["rad","rad"] for direction and [""] for Stokes. See #1002 and #1819.

    FITS import with independently placed spectral and Stokes axes¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 writes a two-axis image with Stokes followed by frequency in pixel order and frequency followed by Stokes in world order. The FITS PC matrix has zero diagonal and unit off-diagonal terms. The same CASA build segfaults in image.fromfits when opening its output.

    casa-rs pairs the world rows with their pixel columns using the PC matrix before parsing the local coordinate models. Imported pixels keep the FITS array order and the native record retains the original world order. The regression reads files written by CASA and by casa-rs and independently checks which pixel step moves each world coordinate. See #1002 and #1823.

    Coordinate subimage with a sampled frequency axis in units other than Hz¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 resamples a tabulated spectral axis in the input coordinate's display units, then uses those values to construct a coordinate in Hz. For example, a sample at 1020 MHz becomes 1020 Hz in the returned record. The rest frequency also loses its unit scale. casa-rs converts the samples and rest frequency to Hz before building the subimage record.

    An explicit negative length for a sampled spectral axis can abort CASA when the signed length is used for an unsigned allocation. casa-rs raises RuntimeError before allocating sample storage.

    When the spectral axis is in different positions in pixel and world order, CASA indexes the world increment vector with the spectral pixel position. Cropping a [10, 11, 13, 18] Hz table to its final two pixels can change a linear axis's increment from 2 to 5 and leave the spectral samples at [13, 15.6667] Hz. casa-rs preserves the linear increment and stores the sampled spectral values [13, 18] Hz.

    CASA also reads byte-swapped NumPy origin arrays as native-endian bytes. For example, np.array(1.5, dtype=">f8") applies a zero-pixel shift on a little-endian host. casa-rs reads the declared byte order.

    FITS export shifts the zenithal polynomial coefficients¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 starts the ZPN coefficients at latitude-axis PV i_1 when it exports an image. FITS WCS defines the constant coefficient at PV i_0. For a polynomial beginning [0.02, 1, 0.1, -0.02], reopening the export in CASA changes the sky positions. A zero constant can cause CASA to reopen the file as a linear coordinate. casa-rs writes the coefficients from PV i_0. Both readers recover the original sky positions from that header.

    A rejected latitude edit can leave a projected coordinate unusable¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, a CEA coordinate with zero reference latitude and LONPOLE=0° cannot move its reference to -0.5 radians with the same pole. coordsys.setreferencevalue raises for this edit but leaves the new latitude in the coordinate record. The same failure occurs for other projections when the requested latitude cannot use the existing pole. casa-rs checks the pole before committing the reference edit and preserves the usable coordinate if the edit fails.

    A display frame can shift an adjusted native coordinate reference twice¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14's coordsys.setreferencecode can pass the displayed reference position into the conversion as if it were still in the native frame. For a J2000 reference of [24°, 32°], adjusting to ECLIPTIC gives about [0.597567, 0.356488] radians. With a Galactic display layer active, it instead gives about [2.582935, -0.784427] radians. An active BARY display layer also changes the result of an LSRK-to-GEO adjustment of the same spectral reference pixel. casa-rs uses the native direction and native reference-pixel frequency, then resets the display layer on the coordinate whose native code changed.

    A rejected combined conversion-frame request changes the direction frame¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 applies the direction conversion in coordsys.setconversiontype before it validates the requested spectral frame. With direction="GALACTIC" and spectral="invalid", the call raises after changing the direction conversion. casa-rs preserves both conversion layers when the call fails.

    Rebuilding a sampled spectral axis can relabel its rest frequency¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 passes the old rest-frequency number to the new setspectral table in Hz. If the old coordinate declares MHz, a rest frequency of 1420.405751786 MHz becomes 1420.405751786 Hz. casa-rs converts the active rest frequency to Hz before building the new frequency or velocity table.

    The same setter accepts a positive rest quantity with incompatible units, such as 21cm, and records it as 0.21 Hz. It can also store an infinite rest frequency. casa-rs rejects these inputs while preserving the prior spectral coordinate.

    Reflected Quality pixels keep their original labels in CASA¶

    For a Float image of shape [3, 2] with a linear axis and a Quality axis ordered DATA, ERROR, CASA 6.7.6.14's image.transpose(order="-10") places the error pixels first but labels them DATA. casa-rs reverses the labels with the pixels and retains their association after reopening the image.

    FITS export can abort on an image with a native Quality coordinate¶

    Exporting a Float native image with a two-plane Quality coordinate (DATA and ERROR) with image.tofits terminates pinned CASA 6.7.6.14 with a floating-point exception. With the Quality axis removed from the public layout and the ERROR plane fixed in the record, export terminates with a segmentation fault. casa-rs raises a Python error and preserves the image in both cases. Its single-HDU FITS writer cannot represent the data and error semantics of a native Quality coordinate.

    Mixed conversion of a nested coordinate system can crash¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 restores a two-axis Linear coordinate system stored as an outer coordsys0 coordinate. With child units m and s, both coordsys.convert([6.0, 7.0], unitsin=['pix', 'pix'], unitsout=['cm', 'ms']) and the equivalent convertmany([[6.0], [7.0]], ...) segfault. Casa-rs raises a Python error and leaves the coordinate record usable. Scalar and batched toworld and topixel continue to use the nested transform.

    The same CASA version can also segfault in coordsys.summary(list=False) when a nested Linear system retains two pixel axes but its inner worldmap0 removes one world axis. Casa-rs reports the incompatible axis counts and leaves the coordinate tools usable for transformation.

    An empty nested list crashes coordsys.convertmany¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 exits with a segmentation fault when a two-axis coordinate system receives convertmany([[], []]). The equivalent NumPy array with shape (2, 0) returns an empty double array of that shape. casa-rs returns the same empty array for both representations.

    Invalid slice indices can terminate image.getslice¶

    On a [7, 8, 3] image, CASA 6.7.6.14 aborts on getslice([0, 2], [0, 2], coord=[0, 0, 100]). Its axis-vector reader also accesses the second entry when an explicit list contains only the first axis. casa-rs raises a Python error for an out-of-range fixed coordinate or a missing second axis and preserves the attached image. An explicit npts=None also aborts CASA. casa-rs raises a type error for that argument.

    image.transpose can change the metadata of a reflected sample¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, reflecting an axis negates the corresponding world increment. In a [4, 6, 5] image with a direction matrix [[1, 0.2], [-0.3, 1]], transpose(order="2-01") moves the sample at [1, 2, 3] to [3, 2, 2] and changes its reported direction. casa-rs reflects the matching pixel column of the coupled transform and preserves the sample's world position.

    For a [4, 5, 2, 6] image, transpose(order="-30-21") reverses the spectral and Stokes samples but retains the original beam grid and Stokes labels. casa-rs moves each sampled plane with its original label and restoring beam.

    For a six-pixel tabular axis with pixels [0, 1, 3, 5] and worlds [100, 101, 111, 120], the reflected pixel 1 represents the original pixel 4. CASA reports 119 there. casa-rs reflects the lookup grid and reports the original interpolated value of 115.5.

    If an image has pixel axes [Stokes, Frequency] and world axes [Frequency, Stokes], CASA 6.7.6.14 reflects Stokes pixels for the named order ["-Frequency", "Stokes"]. casa-rs resolves the names through the world-to-pixel mapping, so this order reflects the frequency planes.

    Unequal image-section strides can shift coupled sky coordinates¶

    On a SIN direction plane with reference pixel [0, 0] and PC matrix [[0, -1], [1, 0]], CASA 6.7.6.14 applies a stride of [2, 1] by doubling the first world increment. It reports about one arcminute of declination change between output pixels [0, 0] and [1, 0]. The selected input pixels [0, 0] and [2, 0] are about two arcminutes apart. This affects the section geometry used by image.subimage, image.pad, and image.pbcor. casa-rs scales the PC matrix with the increments so that each selected pixel retains its sky position.

    Fluxscale dictionaries can select the wrong windows in setjy¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 documents spw as a selector for valid windows in a fluxdict. Its Python wrapper calls ms.msseltoindex on the class when spw is explicit, raising AttributeError before writing. With an implicit selection, all fluxd=-1 and a nonzero fitted flux, the wrapper passes an empty window list. The imager interprets it as every window and can replace an existing model. casa-rs applies the intersection of the selected window IDs and the valid dictionary entries. An empty intersection leaves the scratch and virtual models intact.

    A fluxscale(fitorder=0) dictionary can also contain only the fitted intercept in spidx. CASA's wrapper indexes the first element after removing that intercept and can raise IndexError. casa-rs uses zero spectral index for this constant fit. The local oracle compares the corrected cases with equivalent CASA manual models and checks preservation of the input model. #1519

    Listing the Butler–JPL Horizons 2010 objects in setjy raises before displaying them¶

    With listmodels=True and standard="Butler-JPL-Horizons 2010", CASA 6.7.6.14 calls an unavailable logsink.posta method and raises AttributeError. The object names are already defined in the task. casa-rs displays that list and returns the empty listing result without opening a MeasurementSet. #1519

    A resolved setjy model uses the wrong manual spectral law¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, setjy(standard="manual", model="3C286_L.im", fluxdensity=2.4, spix=-0.74, reffreq="1.41GHz") writes zero visibilities in the 1.413 GHz VLA band. With spix=0, scalebychan=True and the default 1 GHz reference, CASA incorrectly gives the image a frequency-dependent amplitude. The resolved-image branch evaluates the spectral polynomial at a frequency in Hz and uses the result as a power of the frequency ratio. casa-rs evaluates the documented polynomial in log10(f / f0), as used by the manual point-source model. It normalizes the existing image morphology to that intensity per channel or at the representative frequency for constant scaling. #1519

    CASA uvsub drops the second feed basis of a resolved virtual model¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, an MS with RR/LL on one window and XX/YY on the next can hold two valid SetJyGridFT records for a resolved IQUV image. ms.uvsub uses the first window's circular model and subtracts zero on the linear window, even when CASA itself wrote both records. Scratch setjy predicts nonzero visibilities on both windows. casa-rs reads either writer's records and applies the matching Fourier grid on each window. #1519

    getcalmodvla rejects a documented calendar reference date¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts a YYYY-MM-DD observation date but raises TypeError for the same refdate format. It parses the date into MJD and then tests the original string against zero. casa-rs uses the parsed MJD to decide whether to include refdate in the request and keeps the supplied calendar date in the component list provenance. #1519

    Convolution can produce isolated infinities in an otherwise undefined plane¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 spreads an unmasked NaN through the FFT axes in image.convolve. The validity mask and planes along degenerate kernel axes are independent. For an unmasked infinity, a four-pixel input [1, 1, 1, inf] with kernel [1, 0, 0] and scale=1 produces [nan, nan, inf, nan]. The surviving infinity depends on the transform and padding. Casa-rs returns NaN throughout the affected plane when convolution mixes a valid nonfinite value, so the result is consistent across direct accumulation, FFT blocks, and tile sizes. A kernel with no active axes still applies the scalar coefficient with IEEE arithmetic. Masked samples contribute zero and the output retains the selected input validity.

    Solar System setjy drops a scan or time restriction¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 uses the requested scan to choose the epoch for setjy(standard="Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012") but omits the scan when writing MODEL_DATA. Even when one scan has been selected, the task replaces existing models in other scans of that field and spectral window. With a time range, it writes the correct rows but calculates the spectrum at the first timestamp outside the requested range because it passes timerange where the CASA tool expects time.

    casa-rs uses the scan and time selection both for the model epoch and for writing. A pinned comparison checks the selected scan against CASA and verifies that unselected model cells retain their previous values. A second comparison physically selects the requested time range in the CASA reference MeasurementSet and checks both the returned flux and complex model visibilities.

    Solar System setjy changes the integrated flux for reversed channel widths¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 passes the two channel edges in reverse order to its brightness integrator when CHAN_WIDTH is negative. For a Titan channel centered at 345.9 GHz with a 1 GHz bandwidth, the reported flux changes by more than ten percent when only the width's sign is reversed. A one-channel spectrum also changes its reference edge.

    casa-rs integrates the physical band from its lower to its higher frequency. A paired one-channel check compares both signed widths with CASA's positive-width result, including the model published to the MeasurementSet.

    setjy fails to read an observation selector supplied as a string¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 assigns its local observation selector only for non-string values when usescratch=True. For example, observation="1" raises before selecting a row, while observation=1 reaches the same documented selector. casa-rs resolves either form. The 2012 Solar System comparison uses the integer form in CASA and the string form in casa-rs against an MS with two observatory rows.

    imager.setjy can abort when the manual reference frequency is omitted¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 can terminate the Python process when imager.setjy(fluxdensity=[5, 0.6, 0.2, 0.1], standard="Perley-Butler 2017") uses the declared empty reffreq default. The binding constructs a spectrum with a zero reference frequency, which the component library rejects.

    casa-rs supplies the task's 1 GHz reference when the tool parameter is omitted. The fixed-flux comparison uses that explicit frequency in CASA and the default in casa-rs.

    An empty imager.setjy selection can widen the next ft¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, imager.setjy(field="0", scan="999", ...) returns a format-only record when the scan matches no data. The call also rebuilds the visibility iterator over the full MeasurementSet. A subsequent ft can then replace model cells outside the preceding selectvis.

    casa-rs preserves the existing selection when the new scan matches no rows. A paired test verifies the format-only return, unchanged model cells for the empty call, and the scope of the following ft.

    Image decomposition counts masked emission and fits empty backgrounds¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 counts masked samples in image.decompose. On a 9 × 11 Float image with peaks 7 at [1, 2], 1 at [3, 4], and 4 at [5, 6], decompose(simple=True, threshold=1, fit=False) returns three islands after its default mask excludes [1, 2]. An expression mask accepting only the 7 peak also leaves all three bounds. The native decomposer reads raw pixels from the selected subimage. Casa-rs combines the default and requested masks with the selected region before thresholding so excluded samples cannot become sources.

    On an 11 × 13 zero image, CASA reports zero regions with decompose(simple=True, fit=True, threshold=0.7), then starts fitting 143 components to the background. Casa-rs returns empty component and bound matrices when the detection set is empty.

    A fit can also be underdetermined. Three samples with values 9, 3, and 1 at [7, 7], [8, 7], and [8, 8] constrain fewer than the six parameters returned for a 2D Gaussian. With threshold=0.7, maxretry=0, and maxrms=0.0001, each implementation reconstructs all three samples to within 0.00001. The independent solvers can select different centers, widths, and angles from the valid solutions. Casa-rs also uses a fixed retry sequence so fits with identical inputs are reproducible.

    predictcomp leaves requested figures unwritten¶

    With CASA 6.7.6.14, a valid antennalist, showplot=True and a nonempty savefig return a component list and savedfig=None. The task produces no figure. This also leaves the documented marker, axis and legend controls without an effect. casa-rs projects the specified array at the observation epoch, evaluates the model's visibility amplitudes at the requested frequencies, and renders the requested figure.

    predictcomp 2012 scales the disk position angle as arcseconds¶

    The Horizons 2012 helper passes the ephemeris NP_ang model angle, in degrees, to componentlist as arcseconds. For Jupiter at MJD 60000 this stores an angle of about 0.0931 degrees instead of about 335.11 degrees. casa-rs uses the ephemeris angle in degrees, as for the 2012 setjy model. This preserves the projected disk orientation when the table is used to predict visibility amplitudes.

    predictcomp can reuse stale task output for a rounded epoch¶

    The CASA task removes a previous component list using a filename formed from the full Python frequency and epoch strings. The imager generates its filename with six significant digits. For repeated 3C286 predictions at MJD 58000.25 with the same first frequency, changing the final frequency can leave the old spectrum in place while the task reports the new frequency grid. The casa-rs task replaces a prior component list at the generated path after completing its new table.

    A circular deviation window with an all-true footprint can abort¶

    On a 15 × 17 Float direction image, CASA 6.7.6.14 terminates the Python process with a segmentation fault during image.deviation(xlength=3, ylength="", stattype="npts"). The 1.5-pixel radius includes all nine pixel centers of the bounding square, so there is no footprint mask. The diagnostic assumes it exists when reporting the circle size. Casa-rs computes the documented circular statistic and clips the window at the image's edges, returning counts of 9 in the interior, 6 at an edge, and 4 in a corner for an unmasked image.

    Image FFT can use the wrong explicit axis or abort on a coupled coordinate¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 indexes its array of requested FFT axes with the requested axis value itself. On a 7 × 8 linear image, image.fft(axes=[1], complex=...) can transform the first axis. The requested value 1 is outside the one-entry list. Casa-rs transforms the requested second axis and rejects axes outside the image's rank before creating outputs.

    CASA can also terminate the process when only one axis of a coupled linear coordinate is selected. A 7 × 8 image with linear transform [[1, 0.2], [0.5, 1]] and fft(axes=[0], complex=...) reproduces it. The linear-coordinate Fourier operation rejects the partial inversion, after which the tool dereferences the absent coordinate. Casa-rs returns the coordinate error and leaves the output destinations untouched.

    For a Fourier transform of a linear frequency or time coordinate, CASA 6.7.6.14 labels the output in seconds or hertz and uses the input's unconverted increment. A four-pixel axis with 2 MHz spacing produces 0.125 s, while the same axis expressed as 2,000,000 Hz produces 1.25e-7 s. A four-pixel axis spaced by 2 ms likewise produces 0.125 Hz instead of 125 Hz. Casa-rs converts the spacing to hertz or seconds before taking the reciprocal so equivalent inputs give the same Fourier coordinates.

    image.findsources can abort on a transposed plane or an invalid source count¶

    On a Float image of shape [21, 23] with a compact off-center source, CASA 6.7.6.14 finds the source in the original sky plane. After transpose(order="10"), the default point search aborts with a heap error in a separate process. SkyComponentFactory::encodeSkyComponent swaps flux and the first position on a latitude-first sky plane and accesses the sixth parameter even for a three-parameter point source. A transposed four-axis image with two singleton axes can instead return an incorrect sky position. Casa-rs maps both pixel positions and ellipse endpoints through the direction coordinate's axis order. The search area still uses the selected image's pixel order.

    A search on a Float image with an unselected third nondegenerate axis aborts with Slicer error:IPosition-lengths differ in CASA, which uses a two-dimensional slice after dropping singleton axes. Casa-rs requires a two-dimensional sky plane and reports a Python error before reading pixels if more than two nondegenerate axes remain. Selecting one channel or polarization before the search still works.

    nmax=0 crashes CASA because the search accesses an empty result matrix. Casa-rs returns an empty component list. A negative count aborts on CASA's negative matrix dimension and raises a Python error in casa-rs.

    The first two mask rows initialize inDone from the mask instead of its inverse. On a 16 × 17 Float image with a compact peak centered at row 1 or 2, CASA finds no source with an all-true mask. When the first two rows are masked off, CASA reports the source anyway. Casa-rs preserves the regular scan starting at row 3 for both masks, so rows excluded by the mask cannot contribute to these detections.

    For a native J2000 sky coordinate with its conversion type set to Galactic, findsources returns Galactic longitude and latitude, approximately (1.68201, -1.05039) radians for an off-center point in a synthetic image centered at J2000 zero. CASA tags these values as J2000, so a component list using that record interprets a different sky position. Casa-rs tags the angles with the frame used to compute them. Gaussian directions and their position angles are computed in that same frame.

    image.fitcomponents writes fitted estimates in the wrong pixel grid¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, fitting a Gaussian centered at pixel [14.2, 17.7] in a 31 × 34 image with the default sky coordinates reports the correct pixelcoords in the fit record. The same call writes 14.9998, 17.0002 in the newestimates file. ImageFitterResults::writeNewEstimatesFile inserts the component direction in radians into a coordinate system whose world values use the visible direction units. Casa-rs writes the fitted center in the original input pixel grid, which is what the estimates-file reader expects.

    The detailed fit record also inherits the direction-label mismatch described for findsources. With a J2000 sky coordinate and a Galactic conversion frame, CASA returns the fitted direction near (1.68200, -1.05040) radians tagged J2000. Casa-rs labels the fitted direction with its conversion frame.

    The optional summary labels the frequency column GHz but writes raw world values. The default spectral axis reports channel 1 as 1.415e+09 under that heading, while the component's frequency record correctly reports 1.415 GHz. Casa-rs converts the summary column to GHz.

    A masked value of 100 next to a 7 Jy/pixel Gaussian gives a reported peak uncertainty of 1.7604 Jy/pixel without a residual output in CASA 6.7.6.14. Requesting that output gives about 3.4e-9 Jy/pixel for the same fit. CASA uses all entries in its anonymous residual image for the first RMS and honors the source mask for the second. Casa-rs computes fit uncertainties from valid pixels whether or not a residual image is written.

    When fitting Stokes Q or U in a multi-Stokes cube, CASA 6.7.6.14 reports the selected polarization's fitted flux but writes its model and residual pixels to the first polarization plane. A rank-five image with an ancillary axis selected at pixel 1 shows the same mismatch. The output write position is initialized to zero and only the spectral position is updated. Casa-rs writes the fitted result to the selected polarization and ancillary position. The input grid and validity mask remain present in both requested images.

    image.fitprofile can mislabel or leave part of a fitted spectrum¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, collapsing the spatial axes of a cube centered on J2000 zero can place the averaged spectrum near the antipode. On a 5 × 7 × 27 synthetic line cube the direction record reports a right ascension of 12 hours. With default detailed logging the inverse projection can fail and the call raises even though the spectral fit converged. Casa-rs uses the original direction coordinate evaluated at the selected spatial pixel midpoint, including for its model and residual products.

    In the same process, fit an 11-channel spectrum with a model image and then reject a fit to a 23-channel spectrum using an amplitude range. CASA's failure buffer keeps the first call's 11-channel shape. Only the first 11 channels of the rejected model are NaN and masked. A later shorter fit can instead attempt a slice larger than its output. Casa-rs uses the current spectrum's shape to mark every rejected channel invalid. Profiles skipped by minpts still retain the input pixels and mask in the products.

    A log-transformed polynomial with every coefficient fixed crashes CASA during fitting. Casa-rs evaluates the given coefficients in log space and reports their zero parameter errors without trying to estimate a covariance. Pixels outside the log function's domain remain masked.

    For an explicit direction-axis fit on a spectral cube, CASA rejects the fit with The X vector must have some elements even though the box supplies 23 pixels on the requested axis. The spectral-axis branch precomputes its abscissa and the alternate-axis branch fails to supply one. Casa-rs derives the fit abscissa from the requested pixel axis and reports its center and width in that axis's world units.

    With a Galactic conversion frame on a J2000 image, the angles in the fitprofile direction record are Galactic but CASA labels and formats them as equatorial. Casa-rs reports the conversion frame and displays its longitude and latitude in degrees.

    CASA calculates the reported integral uncertainty by multiplying relative errors by the signed line integral. A fitted absorption line therefore has a negative uncertainty. Casa-rs preserves its negative integral and reports the standard error as a nonnegative magnitude.

    For a Gaussian multiplet with tied peaks of 6 and 3 and an accepted amplitude range of 4 to 7, CASA accepts both peaks because its constraint loop repeatedly examines the first peak. Casa-rs checks the range against every component of the multiplet.

    A synthetic Gaussian centered at channel 15 with its peak and width fixed gives a different center in CASA after its peak and sample values are scaled from 1 to 10⁻¹⁵. The velocity center shifts by about 0.0175 km/s. Casa-rs scales the solver's damping to its curvature and fits the same physical center at both intensities.

    image.getprofile can return values on a different axis than requested¶

    On a 4 × 5 × 1 × 7 image, CASA 6.7.6.14 returns the right pixels for a region selecting channels 1 through 5, but with frame="BARY" its reported frequencies come from channels 0 through 4. The conversion uses the original coordinate system with channel numbers starting at zero. Casa-rs converts the actual selected channels and pairs their coordinates with the corresponding reduced samples.

    A declination profile on the same image can fail an AlwaysAssert newWorldOrder.nelements() == nWorldAxes() when a world unit is requested. Casa-rs keeps the selected declination axis and evaluates its coordinates along the spatially collapsed image grid.

    With spectype="beta" and unit="m", CASA reports its unchanged frequency values while labeling them as meters. Casa-rs rejects relativistic velocity with a wavelength unit, as it does for radio and optical velocity.

    For a region retaining channels 1, 3 and 5, CASA returns samples at those channels but numbers the planes array 1, 2 and 3. The same contiguous numbers appear in coords when pixel units are requested. Casa-rs reports the original sampled pixel numbers.

    image.histograms can abort on duplicate axes¶

    On a 5 × 3 Float image with axes=[1, 1], CASA 6.7.6.14 aborts inside the lattice collapse. It checks each axis in isolation and passes a duplicated axis to the tile iterator. Casa-rs raises a Python error for duplicate axes and keeps the image attached and its pixels intact.

    image.maxfit can select the wrong channel or crash on an all-masked image¶

    On a direction cube with peaks of +6 in one channel and +2 and −12 in another, CASA 6.7.6.14 returns the weaker positive source with negfind=False and the +6 source with negfind=True. The plane-selection branch applies the opposite sign policy to the one documented, and the subsequent source search can miss a negative peak. Casa-rs ranks positive peaks by value by default and ranks both signs by magnitude with negfind=True, retaining the fitted peak's sign. It ranks fit-eligible peaks by their sampled pixel values. A broad source with a larger fitted height cannot replace a sharper source whose sampled peak is stronger. The fit can resolve an extremum between two equally bright adjacent pixels.

    image.moments can report an extreme channel in the wrong Doppler convention¶

    On a spectral cube with nine monotonically increasing channel intensities, a rest frequency of 1.1 GHz and observed frequencies near 1.415 GHz, CASA 6.7.6.14 uses optical velocities for the weighted coordinate with doppler="OPTICAL". The median, maximum and minimum coordinates still use radio velocities. Casa-rs converts the selected channel to the requested Doppler convention for every coordinate-valued moment.

    On a one-axis tabular image with world coordinates [3, 4, 10, 14, 64, 80], a region retaining pixels 1, 3 and 5 should carry world coordinates [4, 14, 80]. CASA 6.7.6.14 uses different coordinates for the weighted and maximum-coordinate moments and the output reference pixel. Casa-rs preserves the world coordinates evaluated at the original selected pixels.

    Collapsing the Stokes axis of a cube with distinct restoring beams per polarization raises a restoring-beam error in both implementations. CASA can create the named output directory before it raises. Casa-rs checks the beam count before publishing any output image.

    With a Gaussian smoothing width of zero and an inclusion interval, CASA can produce a moment image with no valid samples because the smoothing kernel is undefined. Casa-rs rejects the zero width before allocating or publishing an output.

    With automatic noise estimation and an all-zero spectrum, the CASA noise histogram can fail to fit. Its caller then uses a noise variable that the fit did not assign. The pinned build masks the zero spectrum for method=["fit"] and method=["window", "fit"]. Casa-rs rejects a spectrum with no signal before calculating its SNR. Plain clipping still returns a valid zero.

    On an entirely masked Float direction image, default image.maxfit can dereference an absent maximum and terminate the CASA Python process. Casa-rs raises a Python error and preserves the image.

    image.pv can reject a strip with reversed endpoints¶

    In a [24, 26, 2, 5] Float cube with the default sky coordinate, CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts start=[4, 7], end=[16, 7]. Interchanging the endpoints enters the 180-degree rotation path and raises a no-overlap error even though the strip lies entirely inside the image. Casa-rs samples the strip in the specified order, yielding the same values in reverse along the offset axis.

    With the same input axes transposed to [Spectral, Dec, RA, Stokes], CASA raises a coordinate assertion at output creation. Casa-rs writes a readable result with axes [Spectral, Offset, Stokes] and the same sampled values projected into that order.

    When the native world-axis map is permuted independently of the pixel axes, CASA removes the world axis with the same index as the collapsed pixel axis. Some permutations reorder the output, omit an unrelated coordinate such as Stokes, or fail an assertion. Casa-rs removes the world axis associated with the collapsed sky axis and retains the order of the other world axes.

    In a diagonal strip centered exactly on a half pixel, CASA rounds the two transverse endpoints separately. On a default [60, 52, 1, 3] cube, [8, 9] to [45, 40] includes both equidistant rows with width=1. Changing the second image axis to length 54 changes the selection to one row. Other half-pixel centers can construct an inverted region and fail. Casa-rs includes both equidistant boundary rows, making the cut independent of low-order rounding and image extent outside the strip.

    image.regrid can extrapolate just outside an integer-aligned region¶

    On a default [31, 33, 1, 7] Float cube, regridding the inclusive box [3, 4, 0, 1] through [14, 19, 0, 5] onto the original coordinate record can mark adjacent rows or columns valid in CASA 6.7.6.14. A sky-coordinate round trip moves those samples across the linear interpolator's boundary by a fraction of a pixel at floating-point precision. Casa-rs uses the exact integer shift on the same tangent plane, preserving the selected region's validity boundary.

    image.rotate can reject an overlapping right-angle sky rotation¶

    For a default [24, 26] direction image, CASA 6.7.6.14 rejects rotate(pa="90deg", method="nearest") with a no-overlap error. The longitude and latitude grids still overlap after a right-angle rotation about the reference pixel. Casa-rs samples the actual overlapping pixels and masks the portions outside the source.

    At pa="180deg" on the same grid, CASA's linear and cubic interpolators can include pixels just outside the top or left edge. A sky-coordinate round trip moves some positions back inside the interpolation cutoff. Casa-rs checks the sky projection and reflects the pixel about the exact reference pixel, so those positions remain outside the grid.

    image.rotate can permute the coordinate axes when dropping a singleton¶

    For a Float [24, 26, 1, 7] cube transposed with order="2301", CASA 6.7.6.14 returns shape [7, 24, 26] from rotate(pa="35deg", dropdeg=True, replicate=True) but assigns Direction, Direction and Spectral coordinates in that order. With per-channel restoring beams, it fails because the spectral dimension no longer agrees with the beam record. Casa-rs retains Spectral, Direction and Direction in pixel order and keeps each beam on its original channel.

    On a default direction image of shape [1, 26], CASA 6.7.6.14 can also terminate when rotate(pa="35deg", dropdeg=True) removes one axis of the required two-axis plane. Casa-rs rejects the resulting coordinate geometry with an error.

    image.rotate can replace the only pixel of a linear plane with zero¶

    On a linear [1, 1] image whose pixel is 5, CASA 6.7.6.14 returns zero from rotate(pa="35deg", method="linear"). Both singleton axes are removed from the interpolation pass, leaving the initialized output pixel instead of copying the input. Casa-rs preserves the original pixel, mask and coordinates when the rotation has no sampled axis.

    image.sepconvolve can replace an explicitly selected kernel axis¶

    On a [13, 15] Float image with an impulse at [6, 7], the pinned CASA 6.7.6.14 call sepconvolve(axes=[1], types=["boxcar"], widths=[4]) spreads the impulse along pixel axis 0. The parser assigns -1 while checking the sole axis, so the request takes the default branch. Casa-rs respects the supplied axis and applies the kernel to axis 1.

    The Python wrappers for image.sepconvolve and image.twopointcorrelation also raise a SystemError for tuple-valued axes, such as axes=(0, 1) when the rest of the call is valid. Casa-rs reports a TypeError before creating or replacing an output.

    image.sepconvolve accepts undefined kernel coefficients¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 fills the processed profiles with NaN for a zero-pixel Gaussian width. With width [-2] on a [10, 12] image it can terminate while trying to allocate the kernel. Casa-rs rejects a nonpositive Gaussian pixel width before publishing an output.

    For an even profile length, the Hanning generator assigns symmetric coefficients around the lower middle sample and leaves its trailing coefficient uninitialized. Casa-rs assigns zero to the unused final coefficient. The assigned coefficients retain CASA's normalization and indexing.

    image.twopointcorrelation can terminate the Python process on invalid axes¶

    For a [5, 7] Float image, CASA 6.7.6.14 can fault when a selected axis is negative, such as axes=[-2, 1]. It can also abort on axes=[0, 0] for a linear image. Casa-rs validates that the axes are in range and strictly increasing before creating or replacing an output.

    image.twopointcorrelation can ignore a selected mask or region¶

    On an unmasked [11, 11] Float image whose value is its first pixel index, an external mask selecting values below 5 leaves 189 lags with at least one valid pair. CASA 6.7.6.14 reports all 441 lags as valid. Its correlation loop only checks the combined mask when the selected image has a physical pixel mask. Adding an all-true pixel mask makes CASA honor the selection. The same behavior occurs for a polygon region. Casa-rs applies the combined validity to both endpoints of every pair.

    For a direction image of shape [1, 7] with an all-false pixel mask, repeated CASA 6.7.6.14 calls can also report valid samples near the zero lag. Casa-rs reports every lag as masked because the input contains no valid pairs.

    WVR global phase reversal can miss sparse spectral-window selections¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14's wvr.gcal(reverse=True, spw=[1]) uses the position of each selected window to build the reversal mask. Its writer then looks up that mask by spectral-window ID. A selection containing only window 1 therefore leaves that window's phase unchanged.

    casa-rs applies the global reversal to each selected spectral-window ID. The compact ALMA comparison confirms that the corrected gain for window 1 is the complex conjugate of the ordinary gain, while the installed CASA result retains the ordinary sign. Pinned CASA WVR tool source

    Seeded WVR proposals vary across CASA C++ standard libraries¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 uses std::normal_distribution for LibAIR's proposal sampler. With the same seed, Linux libstdc++ and macOS libc++ return each Gaussian pair in opposite order. The projected draws change the accepted fits. On the original ALMA uid___A002_X8ca70c_X5_shortened.ms fixture with segsource=False, nsol=5, rseed=27, refant='DA41', Linux CASA accepts three fits and macOS CASA accepts four.

    casa-rs uses a fixed draw order on both platforms. The Mac and Linux native posterior rows agree, and the seeded fit agrees with the pinned Linux CASA reference. This keeps native seeded calibration reproducible across hosts. Pinned CASA proposal sampler

    WVR can move successful atmospheric fits into earlier segments¶

    On the recorded ALMA test MeasurementSet uid___A002_X8ca70c_X5_shortened.ms, CASA 6.7.6.14 and casa-rs recover the same two successful atmospheric fits. The other two fits have zero Bayesian evidence. LibAIR's doALMAAbsRet advances its segment-boundary index only when a fit succeeds. SimpleMultiple consequently attaches those two successful fits to the first and second segments even though they measured the second and fourth.

    casa-rs keeps both successful fits at their original times. The oracle reconstructs the CASA and corrected gain tables independently from the coefficients logged by CASA and the recorded radiometer temperatures. The native output agrees with the correctly assigned gains within 2.5e-5 normalized RMS. The incorrect CASA assignment produces a gain difference of approximately 0.123 normalized RMS.

    WVR can dereference a missing single retrieval¶

    For the same recorded ALMA observation, CASA 6.7.6.14 with segsource=False, toffset=-1.0 retries after a zero-evidence fit. In that retry the only selected measurement is flagged. LibAIR's ALMAAbsProcessor returns a null pointer when no fits remain and the tool dereferences it while calculating gains. The paired oracle reproduces the segmentation fault in a subprocess.

    casa-rs returns a failed retrieval with rval=1 and publishes no table. The nearby two-retrieval case with the same time offset has a valid fit and produces the same gains in both engines.

    Replacing a native image alias can mix a peer's pixels and history¶

    Open a Float native image through a symbolic link using one image tool. Then rename a different image over that link using a second tool with overwrite=True. In CASA 6.7.6.14, a first tool that already read pixels keeps reading the original table's pixels, while history() reads the replacement table's history. When its first pixel read happens after the rename, it can also read the replacement's pixels. With the pixel reader already open, the renaming tool can continue reading the peer's cached pixels. Casa-rs binds the peer to its original table and the renaming tool to the moved table. The peer retains the name supplied when it was opened.

    CASA 6.7.6.14 also permits replacing a destination link inside a native table that an image or table tool has open. Casa-rs applies its existing containing-table ownership checks before changing a link. The call returns a busy-table error and preserves both paths, since a link under a table can participate in its live subtable layout.

    Invalid Jy/K factors can publish unflagged nonfinite gains¶

    The pinned CASA 6.7.6.14 gencal(caltype='jyperk') and getjyperkalma convert factors to antenna gains with 1/sqrt(factor). A zero factor writes an unflagged infinite gain. A negative factor writes an unflagged NaN. Casa-rs rejects a factor that cannot yield a finite positive single-precision gain, and any accumulation that overflows or underflows to zero. If the caller supplied a calibration table to update, the original table remains intact. The Jy/K oracle tests the two invalid factors and checks the existing table after the rejection.

    A flagged F Jones coefficient can leave unflagged visibilities¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, a flagged TEC coefficient for the last antenna in a circular-feed F Jones table leaves that antenna's Jones matrix at its nominal identity with both receptors marked valid. Applying the table leaves its baselines unflagged even though a correction is missing. Casa-rs flags the affected correlations when the apply mode writes flags and retains the valid antenna's correction. The TEC oracle exercises this difference using a CASA-written table.

    An empty EOP result can delete an existing calibration table¶

    With an existing Fringe Jones destination, CASA 6.7.6.14 starts by creating a fresh destination. If an input EOP file contains no updates or cannot be read, CASA removes the destination during cleanup. Casa-rs stages a replacement only when it has finished generating a nonempty product. The existing table survives both a missing file and a file with no matching updates.

    EOP interpolation can ignore later daily samples¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 bounds the interpolation index by the number of columns in its Python EOP dictionary. The bound is always three, so an observation after the fourth sample can use two earlier values even when the input covers the observed time. Casa-rs brackets the epoch by the available samples. The seven-epoch EOP oracle checks the resulting delay against an independent ERFA matrix calculation and measures the difference from CASA.

    A zero single-dish sky reference can write an unflagged infinity¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 divides the sky-subtracted visibility by a zero reference spectrum and can publish infinite corrected values with the original channel flag still clear. Casa-rs retains the value entering the sky step when the sky spectrum cannot provide a finite correction and flags the channel in modes that write flags. The paired sky-application oracle checks the zero reference alongside usable channels.

    Raster sky calibration can skip the last strip¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14's raster gap detector tests the next element of an uninitialized boundary array before adding the final integration count. Repeated runs on the same 22-strip map can publish either 44 or 42 solutions. In the 42-solution result both references from the last strip are missing. Casa-rs always includes the last strip and checks its solutions against the selected integrations and the complete CASA runs. Pinned CASA raster source

    Double-circle gain calibration can abort on several selected channels¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 uses a scalar gain cell while copying the selected spectrum into the solve buffer. On the paired total-power map, sdgaincal with spw='0:1~2' terminates with ArrayShapeError because a one-channel cell receives two channels. The same map with spw='0:1' produces scalar solutions at the selected frequency. Casa-rs reports a catchable single-channel requirement before publishing an output. The paired oracle runs the CASA crash case in its own process.

    With the field reference moved outside the mapped region, the same CASA release can segfault when no integration passes the central-region filter. Casa-rs returns a catchable solve error and preserves an existing destination.

    The filter interpolates pointings in time order and applies the resulting selection mask in input order. This can shift the reference samples for physically shuffled input rows. Casa-rs follows that selection and emits solutions in the same spectral-window and time order as CASA.

    Single-dish smoothing can publish an incomplete MeasurementSet¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 creates the output of sdsmooth before it validates the convolution. A partial channel selection whose width has no configured convolver raises an error and can leave a MeasurementSet with zeroed spectra. Casa-rs stages the output, reports the convolution error, and preserves an existing MeasurementSet on a failed overwrite. A successful retry publishes the completed replacement.

    Single-dish baseline tables can contain malformed singleton mask ranges¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 writes an isolated fitted channel as one endpoint when the channel starts a spectrum's mask. Its own apply_baseline_table requires start/end pairs and rejects an odd-length list. Casa-rs writes both endpoints for singleton ranges. The paired baseline oracle applies the resulting casa-rs table with CASA.

    Single-dish baseline weight updates can fail when removing two columns¶

    When both spectral noise columns exist, CASA 6.7.6.14 runs the baseline calculation, then passes the space-separated string WEIGHT_SPECTRUM SIGMA_SPECTRUM as a single column name to table.removecols. The task raises after writing the MeasurementSet. Casa-rs's task publishes the recalculated scalar weights and leaves out both spectral columns. The direct tool retains the undefined spectral columns in its output schema.

    Single-dish baseline reports accumulate clipped-channel counts¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 carries the clipped-channel count from earlier spectra in a visibility buffer into a spectrum's CSV and text report. With one rejected channel per spectrum and two polarizations, successive records can show 1,1,2,2,3,3. Casa-rs reports the number rejected in each spectrum.

    Single-dish baseline fitting accepts negative iteration counts in CASA¶

    The CASA 6.7.6.14 task passes clipniter+1 to the tool, which converts it to an unsigned 16-bit fit count for the solver. A count of zero leaves the input real spectra in the output and can write coefficients and RMS values without performing a fit. Smaller values can wrap to very large fit counts. Casa-rs requires a nonnegative clipniter and a positive direct-tool num_fitting_max.

    Dense single-dish cubic splines can lose numerical accuracy in CASA¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 solves a normal system for the spline coefficients. On a 96-channel input with seeded Gaussian samples, the fitted residuals differed from an independent B-spline least-squares calculation by RMS 0.0557 with 47 pieces and 0.5401 with 93 pieces. Casa-rs solves the design matrix with an SVD. Its fitted residuals agreed with the independent calculation within RMS (2.2\times10^{-8}) on both inputs.

    Single-dish automatic line masks can access invalid channels in CASA¶

    CASA's line finder can call its median helper with zero searchable bins. Its wing extension can also decrement an unsigned index at channel zero. Casa-rs stops an averaging level when it has fewer than two eligible bins and stops the wing at the start of the spectrum.

    Single-dish line fitting can exceed its time bin on descending rows¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 iterates fit_line by data description and the uncombined scan, state, and field keys. SDMSManager::setIterationApproach omits TIME from this sort. The averaging iterator compares later time stamps with its first buffer's time. With physical rows at 6, 4, 2, and 0 seconds and timebin='1s', timespan='scan', CASA combines the four spectra per hand into one. The same input in chronological order produces four spectra per hand. casa-rs sorts the integrations by time inside each grouping key so the requested interval holds for either row order. The paired oracle verifies both CASA results and the native chronological grouping.

    Single-dish polarization averaging can abort for one selected hand¶

    In CASA 6.7.6.14, PolAverageTVI::configurePolAverage obtains its two hand indices from the full POLARIZATION table setup. With an XX/YY MS and sdfit(pol='YY', polaverage='geometric', nfit=[1]), CASA uses the original pair to slice an array with just one selected hand and aborts with ArrayBase::operator()(b,e,i) - incorrectly specified. casa-rs resolves the two hands after correlation selection. When there is no complete pair it uses the selected spectrum unchanged, as the iterator's own skip message describes. The value agrees with fitting the same selected hand without averaging.

    Single-dish line fitting aborts for negative component counts¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 uses std::stoi on the comma-separated list counts and stores them in an unsigned vector. In list mode, nfit=[-1] reaches a negative array shape and aborts outside the task exception handler. casa-rs reports the invalid component count before allocating a fit and keeps the auto-mode interpretation, where the line finder determines component counts.

    A failed line fit can delete the previous report¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 removes an existing sdfit report at the beginning of an overwrite. If a later selection or fit fails, the older report is lost. casa-rs stages the text report and replaces the existing file after successful processing.

    Atmospheric correction can remove an unrelated output directory¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 uses recursive directory removal for an existing sdatmcor destination when overwrite=True. A nonempty directory containing unrelated files is deleted before output is written. casa-rs replaces a readable MeasurementSet or an empty placeholder after preparing the new product. It preserves a nonempty directory that contains no MeasurementSet.

    An empty atmospheric correction window selection raises a record-type error¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 resolves the windows to process separately from the windows to output. With spw='19', outputspw='23' on the upstream total-power fixture, the work list is empty. NumPy infers a floating-point array for the empty list, and the atmcor record conversion rejects processspw before it can write the requested data. casa-rs passes a typed empty list and writes window 23 with its spectra unchanged.

    Atmospheric correction can index a cropped window from channel zero¶

    On X320b_sel2.ms, sdatmcor(spw='19', outputspw='19:370~407^2', scan='7') writes the requested channels. CASA 6.7.6.14 subtracts corrections for original channels 0 through 18 from their data. The paired oracle recovers that exact offset from the uncropped CASA product. casa-rs uses the correction at each selected original channel. Its cropped spectra equal the same channel slice of its full-window correction, including reordered and overlapping ranges.

    Atmospheric correction can publish unflagged nonfinite spectra¶

    With the recorded total-power fixture and CASA 6.7.6.14, a gain table with zero amplitude for window 19 produces an infinite reciprocal-square factor. A scalar factor of 1e40 also exceeds the Float32 range of the corrected spectra. Both inputs write unflagged nonfinite samples. casa-rs rejects either result before publishing the output, preserving an existing product on overwrite.

    ASAP import writes observation times in days to a seconds column¶

    CASA 6.7.6.14 copies the scan table's MJD day range into OBSERVATION.TIME_RANGE, whose unit is seconds. The same import converts the MAIN integration times to seconds.
